item.title: The Young Bucks BULLDOZED In Brutally Short AEW Dynamite SQUASH! (AEW News)
item.description: AEW While the Young Bucks may have retained the AEW Tag Team Titles against the Don Callis Family's Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher at WrestleDream this past weekend, the Bucks were completely decimated by two other Callis Family men on last night's Dynamite. There, Matt and Nick Jackson faced off against Mark Davis and Jake Doyle in a title eliminator match that didn't even last three minutes. From the get-go, Davis and Doyle took control of this one and put a beating on the Young Bucks around the ringside area, with Matt Jackson thrown into a barricade, and Nick Jackson powerbombed through the timekeeper's table. And once the action finally hit the ring, Davis hit Matt with three of his patented piledrivers, as Doyle grabbed a bearhug on Nick. That was the end of the match, as Davis pinned Matt Jackson, and Doyle put one foot on Nick Jackson to get the simultaneous three-count on the Bucks. The story here was that the Young Bucks were coming into this match banged up from their WrestleDream defence against Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher, and they'd only just been cleared to compete. Either way, this victory for Mark Davis and Jake Doyle was one of the most dominant in AEW history, and put the two on course for a shot at the AEW Tag Team Titles at Full Gear on Saturday, November 14th. Likewise, all four of Davis, Doyle, and the Bucks are expected to be involved at Blood & Guts on November 4th. All Future PLC brands are supported by its audience. item.title: Delta traditional rulers mourn Uduaghan
item.description: The Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers has mourned former Governor Emmanuel Ewetan Uduaghan, describing him as a detribalised leader whose legacy of peace, development and support for traditional institutions would endure. The council, in a condolence message dated October 21, 2026, extended its sympathies to the Uduaghan family of Abigborodo, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the people of Delta State over the former governor’s death. The message was signed by the Chairman of the council, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Orhue I, CFR, MNI. The traditional rulers said the news of Uduaghan’s death was received with shock and profound bewilderment, recalling his cordial relationship with the traditional institution during his tenure as governor. According to the council, Uduaghan prioritised the welfare of traditional rulers and made significant contributions to human capital development, infrastructure and the promotion of peace among the state’s ethnic groups. It described the former governor as a detribalised leader who treated all parts of Delta as one indivisible family, irrespective of ethnic differences. The council noted that although Uduaghan inherited the Warri crisis from his predecessor, he worked to establish lasting peace among the three warring ethnic groups. It said his contributions would continue to resonate among Deltans, particularly his efforts to strengthen the traditional institution and enhance its standing alongside similar institutions in other states. The council prayed for the repose of Uduaghan’s soul and other departed faithful, while asking God to comfort his immediate family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state over what it described as an irreparable loss. The post Delta traditional rulers mourn Uduaghan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Leam Richardson Praises Reading’s Defence In 1-0 Leyton Orient Win
item.description: The Royals secured a brilliant 1-0 victory over Leyton Orient at the SCL Stadium to move into the League One play-off places. A second-half strike from Paddy Lane proved to be the difference, although the Royals could have enjoyed a more comfortable victory after Lewis Wing saw his first-half penalty saved. The victory moves Reading up to sixth in the table. Royals boss Leam Richardson spoke to Royals TV to share his thoughts on the performance and another important three points. Richardson on the victory “Yeah, a good response from the weekend. The result, not the performance, but yeah, clean sheets – I love clean sheets! “I thought we worked hard, certainly in the second half. We started the game really well. I thought we were really good with the ball and without the ball, and caused them all sorts of problems. “I think they changed shape a couple of times as well, which is always a good sign of respect. We’re probably disappointed not to go in at half-time one or two goals up. “In the second half, we had to be really good without the ball. Although it looked like they had some good shots, I don’t really remember Joel having to make any massive saves. “I thought we were quite comfortable controlling the ball. We probably started to play the result a little bit for 20 minutes, but that’s human nature. We’re at home and we’re trying everything we can to win. “We made changes to get us back up the pitch a little bit, and the lads who came on did their jobs really well. “The goal was a typical team goal. Our possession, controlling the spaces where we wanted to be, and then in transition, it was fantastic. A really good team goal, so I’m really pleased.” Richardson on Lewis Wing’s missed penalty “Listen, we’ve got good players. We knew there was nothing lost, nothing gained. We’ve got to stay strong with it. “He’s very experienced, Wingy, isn’t he? So I’ve got no issues with that. He’ll take the next one. “He’s disappointed like everybody else, but I thought him and Andy in the middle of the pitch were excellent tonight, with and without the ball. “In the first half, they were fantastic. They made great decisions, changing play, and then I thought without the ball in the second half, the lads were really controlled. “The wide players on the outside, the nine and the 10 in front of them, I thought we were very good.” Richardson on the defensive performance and clean sheet “It’s not just about the back four and the goalkeeper, you need all 11. “You see how hard the lads work for 60 or 70 minutes, controlling where we wanted to put the ball for large parts of the game. I think it’s credit to everybody, all the way through to Joel. “We were very methodical in what we were doing without the ball in the last 20 minutes, so that was really pleasing. “I think we probably deserved the win off the back of our endeavour without the ball in the second half and the way we played in the first half.” Richardson the fans “I’ve got to say, towards the end, I felt

item.title: “It will be so sad” - MotoGP riders lament loss of Phillip Island
item.description: Motorsport photo MotoGP riders have voiced their disappointment at Phillip Island’s impending departure from the championship, with many describing it as one of their favourite venues on the calendar. This weekend’s Australian Grand Prix marks MotoGP’s final visit to Phillip Island, with the series set to move to a revamped Adelaide street circuit next year. The 4.4km circuit has proved extremely popular with the grid, who have been won over by its high-speed layout, frequent elevation changes and old-school characteristics. The atmosphere at the venue located south of Melbourne adds to the appeal of the race, with its coastal setting and scenic views making it a distinctive stop on the MotoGP calendar. As the only Australian on the grid, Pramac’s Jack Miller showered praise on the Phillip Island Circuit and explained what makes the track so special for him. “[The emotions are] pretty high,” he said. “It’s probably one of the most iconic tracks on the calendar and produced arguably some of the best races we've ever seen in MotoGP. “Phillip Island is a track where if you haven't got the bike working amazing, you can still make up a bit of difference once you get the thing round up. Our bike turns pretty good. So as long as we can kind of get it round up and get it turning all right, you should be in with a shout. “This place is phenomenal, and on a MotoGP bike riding around here, it's something particular. You're kind of dancing with the bike the whole way through, trying to manage the shaking, the wheelie and the way the bike deals with the wind. “You can never fully attack. You're kind of just playing with the bike the whole time, which makes it all the more fun to ride. “I thought as ironic as it gets, we'd have fantastic weather throughout the weekend after what we've had the last couple of years with some trying conditions. But it doesn't look that way. Phillip Island is giving itself a proper send-off with some ever-changing conditions.” KTM’s Pedro Acosta said he puts Phillip Island in the same breath as legendary motorcycle tracks like Mugello, as he prepares to bid farewell to the venue. Asked how riders would feel on their last visit to Melbourne, Acosta said: “On one side, it will be beautiful for everyone; and on the other one, it will be so sad. “One of the best atmospheres around the whole calendar, the fans are so close to us. Also, the track is one of these legendary tracks around the championship, like Mugello, Jerez and other ones around. “It will be so sad that next year we don't come here.” Phillip Island track details Phillip Island track details Marc Marquez , a two-time winner of the Australian Grand Prix, described Phillip Island is a track that commands respect from riders. “It’s one of my favourites and I really enjoy it,” he said. “But it’s a very fast, very narrow track, where if you crash, you’re in the gravel in no time. “It’s one of those tracks that riders have a healthy respect for; it’s a bit like Holland too – yo

Also, the track is one of these legendary tracks around the championship, like Mugello, Jerez and other ones around. “It will be so sad that next year we don't come here.” Phillip Island track details Phillip Island track details Marc Marquez , a two-time winner of the Australian Grand Prix, described Phillip Island is a track that commands respect from riders. “It’s one of my favourites and I really enjoy it,” he said. “But it’s a very fast, very narrow track, where if you crash, you’re in the gravel in no time. “It’s one of those tracks that riders have a healthy respect for; it’s a bit like Holland too – you’ve got that respect for it. “The final section is the one that really impresses, especially on the first few laps, and it’ll continue to impress this year.” Marquez’s title rival Jorge Martin also highlighted the appeal of the wider Phillip Island experience, where riders often stay in rented holiday homes rather than conventional hotels. “I'm sure I will miss Phillip Island for the next few years. Maybe we will come back in the future, but for the moment I will miss it,” he said. “First of all, the track itself. It's nice to ride here. It's really different from what we are used to. It's really fast. You need to put a lot of technique to be fast here. Since I arrived here in Moto3, I always loved it. “Then, the place. The vibe here is great. Also, you're in a house with all this wildlife where you can surf and everything. So it's a nice place and I always enjoyed it.” While Phillip Island has a cult following within motorcycle racing, ageing facilities and limited accommodation options had cast doubt over its future for several years. This year, the state government of South Australia secured a new deal to move MotoGP away from Victoria, with the Adelaide street circuit that once staged Formula 1 races gearing up to host the premier class next year. While MotoGP riders have softened their stance on Adelaide after MotoGP allayed their safety concerns with an AI-generated onboard video, they admit they will miss the outgoing Phillip Island. Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing “Phillip Island was always a beautiful race for the show, for the TV and for the fans,” said Honda rider Luca Marini . “In some years, it was maybe the most beautiful race of the year. 2018, 2017, I don't remember well, but the races were unbelievable, and also later on. “It's always the [winners’] trophy; it's unbelievable. It's something that I always dream about, but unfortunately, I was not on the podium here, so let's try in the wet this year. “It will be another amazing trophy because I think it's still one piece with history, with a unique style that you can find. You can win only here, and for the riders, the trophy is always important.” Aprilia star Marco Bezzecchi added: “Normally, at beautiful tracks, you always have very beautiful races. Here the battles have always been amazing. “Last year, the race was fantastic. It was my first MotoGP podium [in Phillip Island] as well. So, it was good.” Phillip Island first hosted the Australian GP in 1989 and became a permanent fixture on the calendar in 1997, replacing Eastern Creek. This year will mark the 30th and final world championship race on the island. item.title: Courtois sends warning to Barcelona as Real Madrid prepare for El Clasico
item.description: Courtois sends warning to Barcelona as Real Madrid prepare for El Clasico Real Madrid kept up their perfect record in this UEFA Champions League campaign as they beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in their third League Phase game. Several players stood out for the Merengue side in this game, but despite the margin with which they won, it was not really an easy game. One of these players who impressed in this game was the goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, as he had to make several interventions, especially in the first half, to keep the visitors from scoring. However, he was still unable to keep a clean sheet as the Germans scored one goal in the second half. As MARCA has reported, the Belgian veteran also talked to the media after the game. He was quite confident for the upcoming game against Barcelona, especially after the team’s recent good run of form: “I think we’ve played some good matches, picked up some good wins and made a great comeback in Rome. We’re confident about what lies ahead, and we know it’s going to be a tough match. But if we want to close the gap in the league, we’ll have to go there and win.” “You never know until you actually play the match. I think we’re in a good place and full of confidence. They’ve been doing very well in the league, but I believe in our team and think we can go there and win. It’s true that we’re playing away from home, and that makes a difference, but I believe in our team. For me, Clásicos are always 50-50, even when one team comes into the match in better form than the other.” The Real Madrid captain put his support behind Vinicius Junior after another underwhelming performance from the Brazilian: “No, I think he’s looking to get back to his best, and I’m sure he’ll get there with the support of the team and the fans. I think he played well. I saw him making dangerous runs and creating threats, but things don’t always go your way. “There are only two players I know of who have been at their best almost every season: Cristiano and Messi. I’ve watched them perform at that level year after year, and even two of the greatest players in history have been criticised at various points. That’s football. I think Vinícius has been playing almost every game for nine years, so we have to help him get back to his best. But he’s the first to be happy, enjoy himself and work towards reaching his best level.” While admitting that Real Madrid have struggled away from home, the goalie also pointed to the team’s improving form ahead of a stretch of away games: “Home and away matches are always different, and we’ve found it more difficult to get results away from home, in places like Spain, Rome and Elche, followed by the two defeats against Betis. I think we deserved more against Betis. We lost, but we played well. “It’s true that we need to improve away from home, but I think we’re doing well now that we’re back after the international break. Hopefully, he will be able to keep a clean sheet in that game, and help the Merengues get a win over their bitter rivals.

item.title: Yobe court sentences man to death for killing wife
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman A Yobe State High Court sitting in Damaturu has sentenced a 45-year-old man, Abubakar Musa, popularly known as Daddy, to death by hanging for the killing of his wife, Ammi Adamu Mamman. Musa was arrested on January 4, 2024, following his wife’s death at New Bra-Bra Estate, Damaturu, and was subsequently charged with culpable homicide, according to media reports. The then Police Public Relations Officer of the Yobe State Command, DSP Dungus Abdulkarim, said the incident occurred at about 4:48 a.m. on January 4, after the ‘C’ Divisional Police Headquarters in Damaturu received a distress call. Abdulkarim said the couple were on the same bed when Mamman was allegedly attacked with a sharp object on the neck, causing severe bleeding that led to her death. He said Musa was arrested for interrogation, while the homicide unit of the State Criminal Investigation Department commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. The case subsequently went to High Court 1 in Damaturu, where the judge reportedly held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. University Community Mourned Deceased Mamman’s death also drew reactions from the university community. A February 2024 newsletter published by Yobe State University identified her as a member of staff and said the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Mala Mohammed Daura, mourned her death and called on security agencies to ensure that those responsible were brought to justice. The university described her death as a loss to its community. She was buried in Potiskum on January 9, 2024, according to the newsletter. The Women-led Civil Society Organizations Network in Yobe State also condemned the killing and called for justice. In a statement issued shortly after the incident, the network identified the deceased as Ammi Adamu Mamman and said she was a volunteer with one of its member organisations. Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, also expressed condolences to the family and called on security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding her death, assuring that anyone found responsible would face the law. A lawyer quoted in media reports said Musa retained the right to appeal the judgment within the period prescribed by law. The post Yobe court sentences man to death for killing wife appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a productive offseason, Yaxel Lendeborg made his debut for the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday. His first task? Try to stop Luka Doncic. It was an unenviable assignment for the rookie forward. But it was also a good test. Unfortunately for Lendeborg, he did not study enough, and Doncic made him pay for it . The Los Angeles Lakers blew out the Warriors, 127-105, at Crypto.com Arena. Lendeborg had 12 points, three rebounds, and two assists in 29 minutes. He was whistled for a technical foul for talking trash to Luka Doncic in the second quarter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In the postgame interview, coach Steve Kerr pointed out the 24-year-old Lendeborg’s learning curve . “This was a great welcome-to-the-NBA game for him. Having to guard Luka, who is as tough to guard as anybody in the world. Having to learn all the little tricks that exist in the NBA. He had three fouls that probably wouldn’t be fouls in any other league in the world. But it’s the NBA. He’s gotta learn this stuff,” said Kerr in the video posted by The Athletic’s Anthony Slater. “It’s his first game. He’s an unbelievable young guy, great talent. It was a frustrating night for him, but a lesson well learned, and he’ll get better from here.” Steve Kerr on Yaxel Lendeborg guarding Luka Doncic in his debut: “He had three fouls that probably wouldn’t be fouls in any other league in the world. But it’s the NBA. He’s gotta learn this stuff.” Kerr didn’t like the technical on Yaxel and not Luka also: “Kind of ridiculous.” pic.twitter.com/SM87XvVY9Y — Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) October 22, 2026 Kerr, who has steered the Warriors to four titles, added that guarding Doncic was “not an easy way to start your career,” although he claimed that the six-time All-NBA got off easily during his verbal spat with Lendeborg. “He (Doncic) kind of lured him (Lendeborg) in a little bit. I thought the single technical was kind of ridiculous. They were jawing at each other. I think it was the words Yaxel chose that got him the T, but then Luka made a half-court shot and got in his face. That should be a tech. Should’ve been a double tech. That feels good, the rookie treatment,” said Kerr with a chuckle. The Warriors will battle the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday. Related: Warriors’ Draymond Green weighs in on Yaxel Lendeborg-Luka Doncic flare-up Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk

item.title: Dangote unveils Pan-African petroleum distribution network, advocates industrial protection
item.description: ……Discloses 25% stake in Kenya pipeline network, projects in Djibouti, Cameroon, Namibia President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has unveiled plans to establish an extensive petroleum distribution network across Africa through strategic investments in pipelines, storage facilities and supply corridors, while urging African governments to adopt policies that protect domestic industries and accelerate industrialisation. Dangote said the Group is aggressively expanding its petroleum logistics and distribution infrastructure across East, Central and Southern Africa as part of efforts to strengthen energy security, improve access to refined products and eliminate longstanding supply bottlenecks across the continent. Speaking during a wide-ranging interview with Financial Times journalist David Pilling, the industrialist disclosed that the Group recently acquired a 25 per cent stake in a petroleum products pipeline network in Kenya and is pursuing additional infrastructure projects connecting Djibouti and Ethiopia, alongside investments in Cameroon and Namibia. According to him, Africa’s aspiration for economic transformation will remain difficult to achieve without significant investments in infrastructure combined with industrial policies that promote local manufacturing, preserve productive capacity and create sustainable employment opportunities. “Allowing imports to displace local production means we are exporting our jobs out of the continent and importing poverty into the continent,” Dangote said. Dangote explained that the expansion forms part of a broader strategy to develop an interconnected African energy supply system capable of linking major refining centres with underserved markets that have historically depended on imported petroleum products and fragmented distribution channels. “We are very aggressive with that,” he said, in response to questions about the Group’s plans for petroleum depots, pipelines and logistics infrastructure. He revealed that the acquisition of a 25 per cent stake in Kenya’s petroleum pipeline network was achieved with the support of the Kenyan government and would significantly enhance the movement of refined petroleum products within the East African region. “Just let me tell you, yesterday, with the support from the President of Kenya, we bought 25 per cent of the pipeline network for the distribution of petroleum products,” Dangote disclosed. item.content:encoded: ……Discloses 25% stake in Kenya pipeline network, projects in Djibouti, Cameroon, Namibia President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has unveiled plans to establish an extensive petroleum distribution network across Africa through strategic investments in pipelines, storage facilities and supply corridors, while urging African governments to adopt policies that protect domestic industries and accelerate industrialisation. Dangote said the Group is aggressively expanding its petroleum logistics and distribution infrastructure across East, Central and Southern Africa as part of efforts to strengthen energy security, improve access to refined products and eliminate longstanding supply bottlenecks across the continent. Speaking during a wide-ranging interview with Financial Times journalist David Pilling, the industrialist disclosed that the Group recently acquired a 25 per cent stake in a petroleum products pipeline network in Kenya and is pursuing additional infrastructure projects connecting Djibouti and Ethiopia, alongside investments in Cameroon and Namibia. According to him, Africa’s aspiration for economic transformation will remain difficult to achieve without significant investments in infrastructure combined with industrial policies that promote local manufacturing, preserve productive capacity and create sustainable employment opportunities. “Allowing imports to displace local production means we are exporting our jobs out of the continent and importing poverty into the continent,” Dangote said. Dangote explained that the expansion forms part of a broader strategy to develop an interconnected African energy supply system capable of linking major refining centres with underserved markets that have historically depended on imported petroleum products and fragmented distribution channels. “We are very aggressive with that,” he said, in response to questions about the Group’s plans for petroleum depots, pipelines and logistics infrastructure. He revealed that the acquisition of a 25 per cent stake in Kenya’s petroleum pipeline network was achieved with the support of the Kenyan government and would significantly enhance the movement of refined petroleum products within the East African region. “Just let me tell you, yesterday, with the support from the President of Kenya, we bought 25 per cent of the pipeline network for the distribution of petroleum products,” Dangote disclosed. The Group is also developing a major petroleum distribution corridor linking Djibouti and Addis Ababa, complete with storage terminals and tank farms designed to facilitate the efficient transportation and storage of refined products. He added that another strategic project in Cameroon is nearing completion, while Namibia has been identified as a critical hub in the Group’s plan to penetrate Southern African markets. Dangote described Namibia as a particularly attractive location because of its strategic proximity to the Dangote Petroleum Refinery in Lagos. “From our refinery to Namibia is just about four days of steaming,” he noted. According to him, refined products from the Lagos refinery will be transported to Namibia and distributed across interconnected markets, including Botswana and South Africa. The Group is also examining other supply corridors extending into Zimbabwe and Zambia as part of its broader objective of developing a continental network supported by strategically located storage and transportation infrastructure. The petroleum distribution expansion complements plans to establish another refinery in Lamu, Kenya, with a projected refining capacity of approximately 700,000 barrels per day. Dangote noted that East Africa’s growing economies, vibrant mining sector and increasing energy demand make the region an attractive destination for refining investments. He explained that the proposed refinery would source crude oil from multiple markets rather than depend exclusively on supplies from Kenya or Uganda, ensuring greater flexibility and long-term operational sustainability. According to him, technical assessments identified Lamu as the preferred location because of its deep-water access, marine infrastructure and availability of critical resources required for large-scale refining operations. Dangote revealed that the investment decision was concluded within four months, although he alleged that vested commercial interests attempted to delay the project through legal proceedings shortly before its public announcement. Beyond energy infrastructure, Dangote strongly advocated policies aimed at protecting domestic industries from unfair competition, arguing that industrialisation cannot thrive if emerging African manufacturers are exposed to unrestricted imports from more established economies. He questioned why African countries should be discouraged from supporting local industries when developed economies increasingly deploy similar measures to strengthen domestic manufacturing and employment. Drawing parallels with recent developments in major global economies, he argued that industrial protection remains a legitimate and widely accepted economic strategy. “If America is now saying, no, we are going to protect our industries, who are we in Africa not to protect our own industries?” he asked. Dangote also disclosed that the Group has earmarked approximately $50 billion for investments between 2026 and 2030, describing the programme as part of a broader mission to demonstrate that African businesses can successfully execute transformative industrial projects at scale. “The legacy we are trying to set up is how do we industrialise our continent?” he said. According to him, the investment programme is designed not only to expand the Group’s operations but also to inspire other African entrepreneurs and investors to pursue ambitious industrial ventures capable of reshaping the continent’s economic future. Looking beyond the energy sector, Dangote identified inadequate power supply, weak financial systems and underdeveloped industrial policies as major challenges constraining Africa’s economic growth. He described electricity as a fundamental requirement for industrialisation, particularly in manufacturing, mining and mineral processing, where reliable power is essential for value addition. With an estimated 650 million Africans still lacking access to electricity, he stressed that addressing the continent’s energy deficit would unlock significant opportunities for job creation, industrial development and economic diversification. Questioning why a continent blessed with abundant natural resources, vast arable land and a young population continues to grapple with poverty, Dangote insisted that Africa possesses all the ingredients necessary to become a major industrial powerhouse. Expressing optimism about the continent’s trajectory, he maintained that Africa’s industrial awakening has already begun. “The journey has started,” Dangote declared. “But now we’re awake, and we will make it happen.” The post Dangote unveils Pan-African petroleum distribution network, advocates industrial protection appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Jamie Carragher tears into ‘disgraceful’ Bruno Fernandes over Man United captain’s Como outburst
item.description: Jamie Carragher has labelled Bruno Fernandes ’ comments on Michael Carrick ’s tactics as “disgraceful” after Manchester United descended into crisis after a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. Cesc Fabregas’ side swept past Carrick’s United with Fernandes visibly upset on the pitch before an outburst at his side’s inability to press. “It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them,” Fernandes said. “But sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.” Th 32-year-old then made a pointed remark that United should have “more brave under pressure,” with the heavy defeat now leaving them 20th in the table after three rounds of fixtures in the league phase and seven games without a win in all competitions. “For Bruno Fernandes to do that, it's a disgrace,” Carragher said on CBS Sports . “When you think about last season, he got player of the year. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick. Bruno Fernandes claimed United should have been braver against Como (Reuters) “Carrick put him back in his rightful position. And he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. “But when you think of him as a footballer, he's a talent. But in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all. And he's reacted like that because he's been brought off. “When he talks about pressing, whether it's man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. “I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard. He's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it.”

Bruno Fernandes claimed United should have been braver against Como (Reuters) “Carrick put him back in his rightful position. And he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. “But when you think of him as a footballer, he's a talent. But in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all. And he's reacted like that because he's been brought off. “When he talks about pressing, whether it's man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. “I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard. He's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it.”

item.title: How Houston Rockets implemented preseason talking points to great success in opening night romp
item.description: Kevin Durant and the Rockets had 29 fast-break points in Wednesday's season-opening win over the Mavericks as Fred VanVleet's return helped unlock a faster-paced offense. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) The two generals, one on the court and the other on the field, faced each other, with one readying for the other's verdict. The former, Fred VanVleet, had just hurled an off-balance pass from his own 3-point line to the opposite end of the court - hitting Kevin Durant in stride for an open dunk. Houston 's point guard turned to his right where the city's quarterback, C.J. Stroud , sat courtside. VanVleet - tilting his hand from side to side - wanted a rating. Stroud gave him two thumbs up. "That's my guy. I don't expect anything less," VanVleet said after the Rockets' 128-110 win at Toyota Center . "I would have been hurt if he would have (given) me a thumbs down." The bucket counted for two of the Rockets' 29 fast-break points - tying their second-highest total from last season, early proof of the faster pace coach Ime Udoka has emphasized through training camp. The Rockets were the second-slowest team in the league last season, forcing them to attack set defenses and often leading to contested shots as the shot clock dwindled. But Wednesday's season opener looked different. Houston shot 52.2% from the field, 44.4% from 3-point range and had assists on 32 of their 47 made baskets. It's just one game against a bad team, but VanVleet's return, offseason additions and a change in tempo gave the Rockets offense some much-needed WD-40 to smoothen the offense. "The ball respects energy and it's contagious," VanVleet said. "So when it's moving and guys are moving and flowing, the shots get better quality and the shots tend to go in more." Playing faster isn't a costless endeavor. Udoka pointed to turnovers and some poor early shot selection as potential tradeoffs. But the Rockets, with VanVleet back on the court and helping limit giveaways, feel they can live with those issues because of the advantages faster pace gets them. Going against a scrambling defense can lead to easy buckets or mismatches as defenders mark whoever is in front of them. Durant and center Alperen Sengun both profited off those "cross-matches." (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) The two generals, one on the court and the other on the field, faced each other, with one readying for the other's verdict. The former, Fred VanVleet, had just hurled an off-balance pass from his own 3-point line to the opposite end of the court - hitting Kevin Durant in stride for an open dunk. Houston 's point guard turned to his right where the city's quarterback, C.J. Stroud , sat courtside. VanVleet - tilting his hand from side to side - wanted a rating. Stroud gave him two thumbs up. But Wednesday's season opener looked different. Houston shot 52.2% from the field, 44.4% from 3-point range and had assists on 32 of their 47 made baskets. It's just one game against a bad team, but VanVleet's return, offseason additions and a change in tempo gave the Rockets offense some much-needed WD-40 to smoothen the offense. "The ball respects energy and it's contagious," VanVleet said. "So when it's moving and guys are moving and flowing, the shots get better quality and the shots tend to go in more." Playing faster isn't a costless endeavor. Udoka pointed to turnovers and some poor early shot selection as potential tradeoffs. But the Rockets, with VanVleet back on the court and helping limit giveaways, feel they can live with those issues because of the advantages faster pace gets them. Going against a scrambling defense can lead to easy buckets or mismatches as defenders mark whoever is in front of them. Durant and center Alperen Sengun both profited off those "cross-matches." Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) puts up a shot around Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington (25) during the first half at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Houston fueled much of that transition attack with another stylistic shift: Aggressive off-ball defense forcing turnovers. Rather than stay on their assignments, especially when guarding below-average shooters, Rockets defenders would move to the middle of the floor to clog driving and passing lanes. Udoka talked about forcing turnovers as a way to "squeeze" more out of an already-elite defense that allowed the fourth-fewest points per 100 possessions last season, per Cleaning the Glass. The Rockets forced turnovers at a bottom-10 rate last season. On Wednesday, the Mavericks committed 21 giveaways that led to 32 Houston points. Houston also entered the season wanting to take more 3-pointers after doing so at one of the lowest rates in the league last season. The Rockets took 36 on Thursday, not an elite mark but still higher than last season's average. The additional shooting opens up opportunities inside. "Last year we started in our backcourt, Twin (Amen Thompson) and Josh Okogie. And a lot of times those guys (were) being left (open) at the 3-point line," Durant said. " … When we got Fred and Marcus Smart out there, who can keep the defense honest at the 3-point line and then twin just roaming around just doing everything … that (puts) everybody in a good position. I think that settled everybody into what they do best." It isn't just about having more shooters. It's also about where they lurk. Jabari Smith Jr., who made four 3-pointers and tied Durant for the team high with 30 points, pointed to Houston's improved off-ball movement, a focus during training camp. The goal, Smith Jr. said, is to keep the defense moving as much as possible. The Rockets were able to implement that change and others to great success in the opener. Now, Houston's goal shifts to maintaining those growth areas moving forward, especially with an imposing test against Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs looming on Friday in Austin. item.title: Maradona doctor was made ‘scapegoat’ for his death, court told
item.description: A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments Wednesday that his client was innocent and had been made a “scapegoat.” Attorney Roberto Rallin rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s November 2020 death was foreseeable, while another defense attorney, Francisco Oneto, maintained that his death resulted from an “acute and unpredictable” heart attack. “There was absolutely no possibility of predicting this fatal outcome,” Oneto insisted. Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Luque, a neurosurgeon considered a key decision-maker for Maradona at the time of his death. “We are here to proclaim Luque’s innocence, not with television slogans, but with the evidence that supports it,” Rallin said. “Leopoldo Luque has been the scapegoat.” Maradona died at age 60 from a cardiorespiratory crisis coupled with pulmonary edema. He was found dead in his bed at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following surgery for a subdural hematoma. The death of Argentina’s favorite son plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. Tens of thousands of people defied social distancing rules to bid farewell to him as he lay in state at the presidential palace. A total of seven health-care professionals have been on trial since April for potential negligence leading to the star’s death during his two weeks of convalescence. Prosecutors have requested sentences ranging from four to 12 years for six of the seven defendants. In its closing arguments, the prosecution condemned Luque’s “inaction,” saying his attitude “was always to do nothing” in the face of the warning signs that Maradona was exhibiting. – Contested medical history – Luque’s lawyers particularly attacked the conclusions of the interdisciplinary medical commission, which had been established by the court in 2021 to provide an opinion on the star’s death. The commission, which based its findings on the autopsy and other things, said Maradona had a history of heart problems that should have been taken into account, a conclusion the prosecution emphasized. But Luque’s defense lawyers said that clinical tests done prior to Maradona’s surgery just before his death didn’t reveal any heart issues. “It’s so clear that Maradona didn’t have any heart problems in 2020,” Oneto said during closing arguments. Throughout the trial, Luque was by far the most combative defendant, speaking several times when he felt he was being implicated. His legal team played audio recordings, presented scientific articles and even a video of Maradona’s autopsy, provoking the anger of the footballer’s daughters. “It’s easy to attack me because I’m the one who had the most contact with Maradona,” Luque said in court, asserting that “the only one who would defend me would be Diego.” “I cared deeply for him, I loved him, he was my idol and my friend,” he said. item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic speaks about his future in LA as the face of the franchise
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Lakers’ Luka Doncic speaks about his future in LA as the face of the franchise appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic isn’t just settling into life with the Los Angeles Lakers ; he is fully embracing the spotlight as the new face of the iconic franchise. Following a dominant 127-105 season-opening victory over the Golden State Warriors, the Slovenian superstar reflected on what it means to carry the mantle for one of the most storied brands in professional sports. Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg tried poking the bear with some second-quarter chatter, but Doncic quickly turned the noise into motivation. He took over the game, pouring in 23 of his 28 points in the first half to put the contest out of reach early. By the end of the night, Doncic stuffed the box score with 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, and three steals in just 30 minutes of action. He was efficient from distance as well, drilling five 3-pointers and dictating the tempo from start to finish. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) When asked after the game about carrying the weight of the franchise on his shoulders and his long-term future in Southern California, Doncic kept it real about how much the opportunity means to him. “Obviously it’s the Lakers, it’s one of the biggest organizations in the world, if not the biggest,” Doncic said. “It’s a lot of honor just to be the face of this franchise. I hope I can stay here long. It doesn’t feel different, but like I said, it’s very much an honor, and I’m just enjoying this moment.” Luka on being the face of the Lakers: "Obviously it's the Lakers, it's one of the biggest organizations in the world, if not the biggest. It's a lot of honor just to be the face of this franchise. I hope I can stay here long. It doesn't feel different, but like I said, it's very… pic.twitter.com/rkZvhqqRJS — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 22, 2026 Doncic showed no signs of feeling pressure on opening night. Instead, he delivered the kind of commanding performance that defines elite franchise pillars. If Wednesday’s masterpiece against Golden State was a glimpse of what is to come, purple and gold faithful can rest easy knowing the future of the organization is in capable hands. Doncic is not merely occupying the throne in Los Angeles, he plans on keeping it for a long time. Related: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk

item.title: Celtic v Celta Vigo – This is a must win match for both sides
item.description: Celtic v Celta Vigo – This is a must win match for both sides Tonight is a must win match for both teams so we can expect an open and exciting contest. A draw is pretty much useless for both teams as both need the three points to kickstart their campaign… Callum Osmand of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Some Celtic supporters see the Europa League as a mere distraction, especially with our main rivals for the title spared the distraction of European football, but it’s still a tournament we should aspire to compete in. Tonight’s opponents are La Liga side Celta Vigo who visit Paradise for the first time on competitive business in nearly quarter of a century, and it will be a tough assignment to earn all three points. Benjamin Nygren of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026 . (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) After losing our first two fixtures and conceding seven goals in the process, it’s vital we kickstart our Europa campaign by snatching a victory, which will not only help our hopes of advancing, it will also give us some much needed confidence in our own ability in regards to competing at this level. Celta will also be of similar thinking as much like Celtic they have also lost their opening two fixtures, and will naturally be looking for a positive result. Kieran Tierney of Celtic celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s first goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) There’s also the financial benefit on offer, with £385,000 available for winning all three points, and although not a fortune it’s still a handsome bonus all the same. But the main focus will be to get back to winning ways on the European front, and try to win back some of our dented pride after two disjointed and disappointing performances and terrible results. Celta of course played at Celtic Park back in 2002 during Martin O’Neill’s star studded sides run to Seville, and won 1-0 courtesy of a Henrik Larsson goal which gave the Hoops a slender win to take to Spain. John Hartson of Celtic celebrates scoring during the UEFA Cup, 3rd Round, 2nd leg game between Celta Vigo and Celtic held on December 12, 2002 at the Campo De Futbol De Balaidos in Vigo, Spain. Celta Vigo won the match 2-1, Celtic won the tie 2-2 on away goals. (Photo by Laurence Griffiths/Getty Images) Celtic would unfortunately lose 2-1 in Spain, but would advance on away goals thanks to a John Hartson strike. A repeat of the Celtic Park scoreline would be most welcome tonight as we look to get our first Europa league points on the board. item.title: Arda Guler jokes about stealing Mbappe’s goal after Real Madrid beat Leipzig: ‘I knew he’d score another’
item.description: Arda Guler jokes about stealing Mbappe’s goal after Real Madrid beat Leipzig: ‘I knew he’d score another’ Arda Guler has revealed why he took the opportunity to score Real Madrid’s second goal in their 4-1 Champions League victory over RB Leipzig , joking that Kylian Mbappe would find the net again anyway. The Turkish midfielder was among Real Madrid’s standout contributors on matchday three and praised his team’s performance both in possession and without the ball. With the European fixture behind them, Guler also made clear that Real Madrid are already focused on the challenge of facing Barcelona in El Clasico. Guler praises Real Madrid’s performance against Leipzig Madrid’s victory provided another positive result in their Champions League campaign, with Guler pleased by the team’s work across both phases of the game. Speaking to Real Madrid TV after the final whistle, the midfielder stressed that the performance was about more than the goals scored. Arda Guler joked about Kylian Mbappe’s goal. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “We’re really pleased because I think we played brilliantly, both with and without the ball. I think we put in a great performance and we’re very happy,” he began. Guler also explained the expectations that come with representing the Spanish giants, insisting that winning must remain the standard regardless of the opponent or competition. “This is what we have to do. We’re Real Madrid, and we have to win every match.” Guler jokes about taking Mbappe’s goal One of the lighter moments from Guler’s interview came when he discussed his goal against Leipzig. The midfielder acknowledged that he had taken the opportunity away from Mbappe, but suggested there was little reason for concern given the French forward’s scoring ability. Arda Guler was crucial for Real Madrid in the Leipzig win. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) “I stole the goal from Mbappe, but that’s because I knew he’d score another one. So, no problem.” The young Turk also pointed to the influence of playing at the Santiago Bernabeu, where the home crowd provides an additional motivation for the team. “It’s a key factor because when we play at home, in front of our fans, we try to give it our all for them.” Attention now turns to Sunday’s El Clasico , with Guler recognising the importance of the meeting and promising that Madrid will be ready to compete for the victory. “It’s a big match, a top-class fixture, and we’ll give it our all to win. We’re ready,” he concluded.

item.title: Mbappe and Arda Guler send strong message to Barcelona ahead of El Clasico: ‘We’ll give everything’
item.description: Mbappe and Arda Guler send strong message to Barcelona ahead of El Clasico: ‘We’ll give everything’ Real Madrid stars Kylian Mbappe and Arda Guler have turned their attention to Sunday’s El Clasico against Barcelona. After securing a 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the Champions League, both players have stressed the importance of the encounter as Jose Mourinho’s side look to reduce the six-point gap in La Liga . Speaking after Madrid’s Champions League fixture against RB Leipzig, Mbappe explained how the squad had deliberately avoided distractions before the European encounter. Mbappe explains Real Madrid’s approach to El Clasico As quoted by FCB World , Mbappe acknowledged that facing Barça carries a different significance from other fixtures. “El Clasico is completely different,” the French forward said. “We were only thinking about the Leipzig match. As for what will happen on Sunday, we can think about it now.” Mbappe is confident of his team putting on a show against Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Mbappe insisted that the squad had not allowed the upcoming Clasico to influence its preparations for Leipzig. “Before that, the team wasn’t thinking about Sunday’s match.” It is the kind of mentality Mourinho always insists on: players should focus on what lies immediately ahead of them. As a manager, he may be forced to consider the Barcelona fixture when making changes to the line-up, but the players cannot afford to get distracted. Arda Guler confident Madrid can challenge Barcelona Guler was equally clear about Madrid’s intentions when asked about the Barcelona encounter. “It’s a big match, a match of the highest level, and we’ll give everything we have to win,” the Turkey midfielder declared. He also emphasised the expectations that come with representing Real Madrid. “We are Real Madrid, and we have to win every match. We’re ready.” For Barcelona, it is a clear message that Los Blancos are completely focussed on the Barça clash and want to give it their best possible effort. Arda Guler has sent a strong message to Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Madrid cannot afford to fall further behind in the title race, particularly with Flick’s side already enjoying a six-point advantage. The Catalan club need to ensure they do exactly that. Barça should put on a statement performance on Sunday to effectively send a message to the rest of La Liga . A victory would extend their lead to nine points and deliver a significant psychological boost after the disappointment against PSG . Sunday’s clash promises to be exciting for both Barça and Madrid fans, and it remains to be seen how the game turns out.

item.title: “It’s not debatable, we can’t go back,” Mbah backs Tinubu on fuel subsidy removal
item.description: …Says “We’ve delivered good governance to Enugu” Governor of Enug State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has doubled down in his support for the removal of fuel subsidy by President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying it was undebatable and inconceivable for anyone to imagine a return to the old order. Mbah spoke at the “Meet the Candidates” town hall meeting organised by Afia TV in Enugu on Wednesday, where he also said that his administration had delivered good governance to the people of the state across all sectors. He described it as a pathetic misconception of the country’s situation and the direction it was headed for anyone to talk about the reintroduction of fuel subsidy. “If you reintroduce fuel subsidy today, we will lose ten times whatever we are currently trying to gain in terms of the removal of subsidy. The poverty rate that you are going to experience will be very high because the naira would be automatically devalued. “We cannot go back to subsidy. And I do not think it is in the interest of the country for us to even debate that. “Again, we should not even debate it because we do not want to send a signal to prospective investors that we are contemplating it. That would take us back. It is going to create panic in the system. It is going to get investors to pull back. “Those that are coming in today to invest in that sector will become jittery. So, it is not even a subject to debate. It is something that we have moved on from, and we should be thinking about how to ensure that the natural benefits cascade to the households, create jobs and generate wealth for our people,” he said. He said the nation should focus on how to further encourage private capital to flow, noting the growth the nation had experienced in the stock exchange space. He added that Tinubu’s policies had stabilised the macro indicators, thus encouraging foreign direct investment. “You can see quite a lot of funds coming into our country, not just portfolio investments, but also direct investments. It is also going to strengthen because the macro indicators are right,” he stated. Mbah maintained that whereas fuel subsidy removal enables the government to target the less privileged, fuel subsidy as earlier practised benefited the rich more. “By the way, I do not think the subsidy we practised before the President removed it was even the right one for the country because even the people we were looking at benefiting from it were only insignificantly benefiting from it. It was largely beneficial to our wealthy folks. “But now, you can almost notice that the government is doing that in targeting the poor, using proceeds from subsidy removal. The government is aggressive on cash transfers. item.content:encoded: …Says “We’ve delivered good governance to Enugu” Governor of Enug State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has doubled down in his support for the removal of fuel subsidy by President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying it was undebatable and inconceivable for anyone to imagine a return to the old order. Mbah spoke at the “Meet the Candidates” town hall meeting organised by Afia TV in Enugu on Wednesday, where he also said that his administration had delivered good governance to the people of the state across all sectors. He described it as a pathetic misconception of the country’s situation and the direction it was headed for anyone to talk about the reintroduction of fuel subsidy. “If you reintroduce fuel subsidy today, we will lose ten times whatever we are currently trying to gain in terms of the removal of subsidy. The poverty rate that you are going to experience will be very high because the naira would be automatically devalued. “We cannot go back to subsidy. And I do not think it is in the interest of the country for us to even debate that. “Again, we should not even debate it because we do not want to send a signal to prospective investors that we are contemplating it. That would take us back. It is going to create panic in the system. It is going to get investors to pull back. “Those that are coming in today to invest in that sector will become jittery. So, it is not even a subject to debate. It is something that we have moved on from, and we should be thinking about how to ensure that the natural benefits cascade to the households, create jobs and generate wealth for our people,” he said. He said the nation should focus on how to further encourage private capital to flow, noting the growth the nation had experienced in the stock exchange space. He added that Tinubu’s policies had stabilised the macro indicators, thus encouraging foreign direct investment. “You can see quite a lot of funds coming into our country, not just portfolio investments, but also direct investments. It is also going to strengthen because the macro indicators are right,” he stated. Mbah maintained that whereas fuel subsidy removal enables the government to target the less privileged, fuel subsidy as earlier practised benefited the rich more. “By the way, I do not think the subsidy we practised before the President removed it was even the right one for the country because even the people we were looking at benefiting from it were only insignificantly benefiting from it. It was largely beneficial to our wealthy folks. “But now, you can almost notice that the government is doing that in targeting the poor, using proceeds from subsidy removal. The government is aggressive on cash transfers. There is also the programme where the government is targeting 1,000 persons per ward across the entire country to be able to provide seed capital for them to become productive,” he added. Meanwhile, on his stewardship so far, Mbah said his administration had kept faith with the people of Enugu State, delivering good governance across all sectors in line with his campaign manifesto. He said the people of the state only needed to imagine where the state was before his inauguration as governor and where it is currently headed. “Let us imagine the Enugu we knew four years ago. Let us just imagine an Enugu without Hotel Presidential. Let us imagine an Enugu without the International Conference Centre. Let us imagine an Enugu without Enugu Air. Let us imagine Enugu without the transport terminals, the 268 Smart Green Schools, 260 Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres. “You do not want them to imagine an Enugu without the International Hospital. You do not want them to imagine an Enugu without the CNG buses, the Nigergas. I think the list is endless. “But I even think that we can stretch that imagination further because the work ahead will be more profound. Just imagine an Enugu where our children are receiving education that prepares them for the world because they have been imbued with evolving 21st-century skills. Imagine again an Enugu where you do not have any part of the city with an unpaved road. “Also, imagine an Enugu in four years’ time that generates 660 megawatts of electricity; where we are able to provide 24-hour power supply; where you cannot come into your house and have the light off; and where people can run their businesses for a whole week without worrying about the cost of diesel. Just imagine an Enugu where you generate electricity and the people of Enugu are buying that at 120 naira because they own the coal that feeds the power plant. “Imagine an Enugu where you now have to ride, not just on our CNG buses, but you have the monorail that can take you from point A to point B. Imagine an Enugu where you can fly from here to the United Kingdom, to the United States and other parts of the world,” he charged the electorate. He urged the people to keep faith with the journey of greatness, growth and development, defending the gains of his first term and guaranteeing the promises of his second term by working for his re-election. “If these imaginations capture our fancy, then we have a duty to fight for it. We do have a duty to continue to make sure that the bar does not come down and that the standard we have set in Enugu is sustained,” he concluded. The post “It’s not debatable, we can’t go back,” Mbah backs Tinubu on fuel subsidy removal appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bayern Munich interested in Kone for January
item.description: Bayern Munich interested in Kone for January Manu Koné is one of the most important players in Gasperini’s Roma. Born in 2001, he is a pillar of the midfield: alongside Cristante, he forms a well-matched duo that combines balance and dynamism. In the final hours of the summer transfer window, Chelsea attempted to convince the Giallorossi to sell the former Borussia Mönchengladbach player, but the Roman club immediately closed the deal. Koné remains one of the Roma players attracting the most interest from the European big clubs. Koné has attracted the attention of Bayern Munich. According to Calciomercato.it, the Bavarian club is particularly interested in the 2001-born player, so much so that they’re attempting to land him as early as the next winter transfer window. For Gian Piero Gasperini and Roma, the player is unsellable, a crucial asset to maintain the balance of a team that is performing exceptionally well. The only way to change this scenario is with a monstrous offer from Bayern Munich.

item.title: San Francisco Giants Advised To Move on From Struggling Veteran
item.description: The San Francisco Giants have a lot of work to do on the roster. According to one columnist, trading Matt Chapman should be a priority? (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty As the San Francisco Giants look ahead to the offseason, should they prioritize moving on from some of their higher-priced players? One columnist says that should be the team’s top priority, with one player in particular singled out. Matt Chapman Labeled as ‘Most Preferable’ Player to Trade Bleacher Report’s Kerry Miller identified each team’s “most likely” trade in the upcoming offseason. Miller named several of San Francisco’s highest-paid players but singled out third baseman Matt Chapman as the one the team should most prioritize. “The Giants still owe Rafael Devers $211M for seven more seasons, Willy Adames $140M for five more seasons, Matt Chapman $100M for four more seasons and Jung Hoo Lee $63M for three more seasons (if he doesn’t opt out of his final two years next winter),” Miller wrote. “Getting out from under at least one of those contracts—Chapman’s would arguably be most preferable—is going to be the offseason goal for a team that has made the postseason just once in the past decade.” The next question is: how plausible would it be to move on from Chapman? Trading Chapman Would Be Easier Said Than Done It’s easy to see why moving on would be considered a priority. That said, several factors complicate things. The biggest possible roadblock is Chapman’s no-trade clause. If Chapman, a California native who has played most of his career in the Bay Area, doesn’t want to be traded, he won’t be. With a full no-trade clause, Chapman would have to sign off on any deal. The same is true for Willy Adames, as well . But even if the Giants can convince Chapman to sign off on a trade, the rest of his contract complicates matters. Chapman is owed more than $25 million a year through the 2030 season. And while that’s a reasonable contract for a top-tier player, Chapman has not been that for the last two seasons. Chapman made a strong first impression in his first year with the Giants. He posted a .247/.328/.463 slash line, hit 27 home runs, had a 7.1 bWAR, won a Gold Glove and finished 11th in National League MVP voting in 2024. The last two seasons, though, have been a much different story. Over the 2025 and 2026 seasons , Chapman slashed .233/.334/.405, hit a combined 28 home runs and missed a total of 112 games. The 2026 season was a particular struggle. Injuries limited Chapman to only 86 games. In that time, he slashed at just .235/.324/.368, adding only 7 home runs. Plenty of teams will pay $25 million for an MVP candidate. But convincing a team to take on a declining player in his mid-30s who’s owed $25 million over each of the next four seasons? That wouldn’t be easy for the Giants. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post San Francisco Giants Advised To Move on From Struggling Veteran appeared first on HEAVY .

That wouldn’t be easy for the Giants. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post San Francisco Giants Advised To Move on From Struggling Veteran appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Verstappen could take a different strategic route in Austin thanks to Pirelli’s tyre selection
item.description: After two consecutive Grand Prix victories, Max Verstappen heads to Austin, where he will face a significant challenge. According to tyre supplier Pirelli, tyre wear could play a major role at the United States Grand Prix. A revised tyre selection does, however, give Red Bull Racing an additional strategic option. Pirelli is bringing three types of dry-weather tyres: the C2 hard, the C3 medium and the C4 soft. As is well known, softer tyres generally offer more grip, but tend not to last as long. Teams must therefore weigh up whether to prioritise speed or run longer without changing tyres. The change this weekend concerns the hard tyre. Last year, Pirelli used the harder C1 for this compound, but this time, it is the C2. The medium and soft tyres remain the same as in 2025, narrowing the gap between the three available compounds. Why the tyres will be under strain in Austin The Circuit of the Americas puts stress on both the front and rear tyres. In the first sector, fast corners come in quick succession, repeatedly forcing the front tyres to steer the car in a different direction. Later in the lap, the rear tyres have to do much of the work as drivers accelerate out of slow corners. This can cause them to overheat and lose grip. The asphalt also plays a part. The section between Turns 9 and 11 has been resurfaced, while the rest of the track surface is getting older. Pirelli expects tyre wear to be a significant factor as a result. Last year, several tyres were heavily worn by the end of their stints. For the drivers, this means that pushing flat out at all times is not necessarily the fastest way to complete the race. Those who ask too much of their tyres early on may lose grip later and start posting progressively slower lap times. They may also need to make an extra pit stop. New tyre selection gives Verstappen an opportunity Pirelli expects a one-stop strategy to be the most likely option. The C2 could play an important role, as it should be capable of completing many consecutive laps. High temperatures could change that plan, however: if the tyres lose performance more quickly, alternative strategies become more appealing. Red Bull will therefore have to judge whether Verstappen can make up enough time on new tyres to offset the extra stop. Staying out longer only makes sense as long as his lap times do not drop off too sharply. Last year, Verstappen won in Austin with a one-stop strategy. item.title: Another Man Utd meltdown! Matheus Cunha & Michael Carrick caught in FURIOUS off-camera row as Champions League disaster sparks dressing room revolt
item.description: Manchester United’s season has plunged into further chaos following a humiliating Champions League defeat that saw internal tensions boil over. Reports have emerged of a heated confrontation between head coach Michael Carrick and forward Matheus Cunha as the Red Devils' winless run continues to haunt Old Trafford. Tensions boil over in Italy The crisis enveloping Manchester United deepened significantly on Wednesday night following a heavy 4-1 away loss to Como. Cesc Fabregas' side dismantled their English visitors in the Champions League, extending United's dismal winless streak to seven matches. Nico Paz orchestrated the rout with a memorable brace, scoring his first inside two minutes to instantly deflate the travelling support. While the result itself was disastrous, touchline developments have sparked even greater concern. According to The Sun' s Samuel Luckhurst , Carrick was involved in a 'relatively robust' altercation with Cunha that television cameras missed. Fans also picked up on the palpable friction between the Brazilian forward and his manager during a chaotic first-half display in Italy. Half-time changes highlight rift The tension between Cunha and Carrick culminated in immediate tactical changes at the interval. The head coach ruthlessly withdrew the Brazilian forward at half-time, introducing Amad Diallo in a desperate bid to inject life into his struggling side. Carlos Baleba was also brought on as United attempted to salvage any pride from the wreckage. These sweeping alterations ultimately proved ineffective. Just four minutes into the second period, Anastasios Douvikas capitalised on further defensive fragility to trigger a relentless wave of attacks from the hosts. Paz soon added his second following a glaring United error, punishing a visiting side that looked completely disjointed and bereft of ideas. The off-camera clash serves as a stark indicator of the rapidly deteriorating atmosphere behind the scenes. With United outplayed in every department, the frustrated exchanges on the touchline highlight a squad fracturing under immense pressure just two months into the campaign. FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Fernandes questions tactical approach The Cunha altercation is merely the latest sign of a broader dressing room revolt. Just a week after Lisandro Martinez publicly slammed the club's hierarchy over a lack of squad reinforcements following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, Bruno Fernandes openly questioned Carrick’s game plan . The Portuguese midfielder expressed clear frustration over the coaching staff's decision to avoid a man-to-man press, claiming it allowed Como to build early confidence. "It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early," the United captain told reporters. "Conceding early makes us go into [the] game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation." Cesc Fabregas' side dismantled their English visitors in the Champions League, extending United's dismal winless streak to seven matches. Nico Paz orchestrated the rout with a memorable brace, scoring his first inside two minutes to instantly deflate the travelling support. While the result itself was disastrous, touchline developments have sparked even greater concern. According to The Sun' s Samuel Luckhurst , Carrick was involved in a 'relatively robust' altercation with Cunha that television cameras missed. Fans also picked up on the palpable friction between the Brazilian forward and his manager during a chaotic first-half display in Italy. Half-time changes highlight rift The tension between Cunha and Carrick culminated in immediate tactical changes at the interval. The head coach ruthlessly withdrew the Brazilian forward at half-time, introducing Amad Diallo in a desperate bid to inject life into his struggling side. Carlos Baleba was also brought on as United attempted to salvage any pride from the wreckage. These sweeping alterations ultimately proved ineffective. Just four minutes into the second period, Anastasios Douvikas capitalised on further defensive fragility to trigger a relentless wave of attacks from the hosts. Paz soon added his second following a glaring United error, punishing a visiting side that looked completely disjointed and bereft of ideas. The off-camera clash serves as a stark indicator of the rapidly deteriorating atmosphere behind the scenes. With United outplayed in every department, the frustrated exchanges on the touchline highlight a squad fracturing under immense pressure just two months into the campaign. FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Fernandes questions tactical approach The Cunha altercation is merely the latest sign of a broader dressing room revolt. Just a week after Lisandro Martinez publicly slammed the club's hierarchy over a lack of squad reinforcements following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, Bruno Fernandes openly questioned Carrick’s game plan . The Portuguese midfielder expressed clear frustration over the coaching staff's decision to avoid a man-to-man press, claiming it allowed Como to build early confidence. "It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early," the United captain told reporters. "Conceding early makes us go into [the] game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation." Carrick swiftly fired back, aiming pointed criticism at his players' work ethic rather than the tactical setup. The 45-year-old labelled the squad's application as unacceptable, bluntly stating: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win." Carrick fighting to save his job FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED Manchester United now find themselves navigating a full-blown crisis both on and off the pitch. With seven consecutive matches without a victory, Carrick faces immense pressure to bridge the growing divide within his squad and restore basic defensive discipline. The glaring lack of on-field effort, compounded by public player dissent, leaves the Old Trafford hierarchy with critical decisions to make. The Red Devils must urgently find a way to halt this alarming slide, or they risk their entire season unravelling before the busy winter schedule even begins.

item.title: Amnesty Int’l demands release of journalist jailed over comments on police
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Amnesty International has demanded the immediate release of 23-year-old journalist Farida Isiak, who was sentenced to four years in prison or a fine of N1.75 million over a Facebook post criticising the police in Kaduna State. The human rights organisation said her arrest and punishment “were clearly because of her attempt to expose abuses by the police.” “Sentencing a journalist to 4-years in prison after a sham trial is a travesty of justice,” it said. Isiak, a reporter with Nagarta Radio in Kaduna, was reportedly taken into custody around 10pm on October 20 by officers under the command of the Divisional Police Officer of Mararaban Jos, Usman Adamu. According to the global rights group, the case began as a minor disagreement between her mother and a neighbour over N100 change during a sale of charcoal. Police first arrested her mother, then detained her father when he went to secure her release, “using their detention as leverage to force Farida to come to the police station.” At the station, officers accused her of defaming them over a Facebook post in which she criticised their unlawful treatment of her parents. Following pressure by the police, she deleted the post and apologised, hoping it would secure her parents’ release. The officers instead kept her in custody and took her to a Sharia Court in Kawo. The presiding judge sentenced her to four years in prison or a fine of N1.75 million for defamation, “completely ignoring the initial police misconduct and the abusive actions that led to the incident.” Amnesty International said: “The arrest, detention, and hasty sentencing of Farida Isiak are a flagrant abuse of power by the police and weaponization of the judicial system to silence free speech and intimidate journalists.” It added that “arresting and holding a citizen’s parents to force a journalist to hand herself over is an unlawful tactic that violates rule of law. Demanding accountability for police actions is a constitutional right”. It called on the Kaduna State Police Command and Nigerian judicial authorities to “immediately release Farida Isiak, drop all charges, and cancel the fine imposed on her.” The organisation also urged the Nigeria Police Force to launch a full and independent investigation into the conduct of the officers involved in the unlawful detention of her family. “Nigerian authorities must stop using defamation charges and the legal system to harass journalists and restrict press freedom,” it said. The post Amnesty Int’l demands release of journalist jailed over comments on police appeared first on Vanguard News .
