item.title: Kawhi Leonard Reacts to His 1st Game Back With Raptors
item.description: Kawhi Leonard Raptors Getty Toronto Raptors superstar Kawhi Leonard reacted to his first game back in Toronto after seven years away with the Los Angeles Clippers. Leonard spent one season in Toronto in 2018-19, and it was a memorable one, as he helped lead the Raptors to the franchise’s first and only NBA Championship. Immediately after winning the chip, Leonard signed a free-agent contract to head back home to Los Angeles and play with the Clippers, where he spent seven seasons, achieving very little playoff success in the process. With the Clippers moving to a rebuilding phase, it made sense to move on from Leonard, especially in the wake of the Aspiration scandal, and Los Angeles traded him back to Toronto this summer. Kawhi Leonard and Raptors Win Against Chicago Bulls On Wednesday night, the Raptors won their season opener at home with a dominant 135-92 victory over the Chicago Bulls . Leonard scored 23 points in 24 minutes of game action in the blowout win. After the game, the always-stoic Leonard spoke to reporters and shared his reaction to a successful return to Toronto. “I’m not really assessing it right now. I never really do. We won the game. Just trying to do what it takes. It’s one game. We’re going to get better. That’s it,” Leonard said. Kawhi Leonard on how he would assess his performance tonight: “I’m not really assessing it right now. I never really do.” “We won the game. Just trying to do what it takes.” “It’s one game. We’re going to get better. That’s it.” pic.twitter.com/T1w4fzeyep — Omer Osman (@OmerOsman200) October 22, 2026 Kawhi Leonard Explains Why He Wanted to Stay on the Floor The Raptors completely blew out the Bulls, so Raptors coach Darko Rajakovic could have easily just sat Leonard on the bench the entire second half had he wanted to do some load management. But Leonard wanted to play and get some minutes in despite the game being out of reach. “I haven’t got a chance to play much in training camp. Any minutes I could get, or continue to play. I know we was blowing them out, but the goal was to try to get 23-24 minutes tonight. I need more reps to learn plays. This is where you get better… You can’t wait till practice and shoot 100 shots. You need game reps. Even on the defensive end, just being able to make calls on the fly instinctively,” Leonard said. Kawhi Leonard on why he wanted to be back on the floor: “I haven’t got a chance to play much in training camp. Any minutes I could get, or continue to play.” “I know we was blowing them out, but the goal was to try to get 23-24 minutes tonight. I need more reps to learn plays.”… https://t.co/bgE77vFbpV pic.twitter.com/dSIcxA7DE5 — Omer Osman (@OmerOsman200) October 22, 2026 This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Kawhi Leonard Reacts to His 1st Game Back With Raptors appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: JD Vance seemingly ignored by slew of Cincinnati Bengals players
item.description: A number of Cincinnati Bengals players walked past Vice President J.D. Vance largely without interacting with him on Wednesday when he visited the team’s practice facility with his son. Vance, an Ohio native and longstanding Bengals fan, made the visit before a midterms campaign rally in support of Republican candidates including Vivek Ramaswamy, who is in a tight battle in the state’s gubernatorial race. In a video posted on X, most of the players were seen filing past Vance without engaging. However, tight end Drew Sample was seen shaking hands and exchanging words with the vice president. JD Vance greets Bengals players on the way out pic.twitter.com/lMKvYRpMfE — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) October 21, 2026 Responding to the clip, the singer-songwriter Bill Madden wrote on X: “This is what TOTAL HUMILIATION looks like: JD Vance attempted to greet Cincinnati Bengals players in the locker room and got snubbed and ghosted by every single player except one.” Dov Kleiman, a NFL commentator, also said: “The Bengals are under heavy criticism online for IGNORING Vice President JD Vance as he tried to greet them. The large majority of the team did not shake his hand or even acknowledge Vance.” Newsweek contacted Vance via the White House press office, and the Cincinnati Bengals’ press office for comment via email outside of regular office hours. Vice President JD Vance speaking at a campaign rally in Sharonville, Ohio, on Wednesday. This is a developing story. More to follow. item.title: Continuing To Improve The Cleveland Browns Heading Towards 2027 - Offensive Review
item.description: theOBR While I regularly write about next season and roster predictions, this looks more at what the team is likely to do. In this piece I want to focus on where the Browns need to improve to get to above average in each position room for 2027. It will focus much more on the starters rather than seeing anything in terms of depth. They have a fantastic amount of cash and draft picks at their disposal to keep adding more to this young talented roster. Quarterback The arguments can continue of if Deshaun Watson is good enough to be a bridge quarterback in 2027 or not, when it comes to winning consistently, it doesn't really matter. Bridge quarterbacks and players you find in free agency, aren't going to take you to the Super Bowl in a loaded AFC. I don't see them going the route of trading multiple picks for a player after how it went previously. So that means the plan will be to take a quarterback next season in the draft. April is far too far away to worry about where the Browns will pick and who the best quarterbacks will be. The season is more about working out if Watson can be the bridge than anything else. Running Back At running back it feels like they need a second back to pair with Judkins in a 1A and 1B scenario like when they had Chubb and Hunt previously. They have plenty of change of pace backs to chose from between Sampson, Sanders and potentially McLaughlin. Luckily it is possible to pick up the type of backs they need in free agency at a relatively decent price. Wide Receiver After years of struggling to get quality at the position, they have three starting quality receivers. They will either need to keep Jeudy next season or add another via free agency, trade or the draft. I would keep Jeudy and then focus on adding more in the draft on day three with the hope you can develop someone. Tight End They need to find more at tight end. While Fannin has plenty of promise he has the potential to be Kyle Pitts type player who can be a massive part of the passing offense but low value in the run game. While they could focus on chasing a run blocking tight end, it will be limiting to have a clear run blocker and a clear pass catcher. This gives a tell to the opposition each time one is on the field. They would be better suited looking to add a more all-around tight end. Even if this effectively moves Fannin to being a hybrid tight end/wide receiver alongside a new tight end, Boston and Concepcion. Offensive Line Everything has been looking very positive on the offensive line over the last few weeks. While people questioned Howard, he has really turned it around and is looking like the $21m a year tackle they traded for. There is a very real chance they run it back in 2027 when it comes to their starters. With four of the starters likely locked in, it is just a question of does Elgton Jenkins return in 2027 or not. As things stand it would be likely but there is a long season to go and he will turn 31 towards the end of the calendar year. Coac

As things stand it would be likely but there is a long season to go and he will turn 31 towards the end of the calendar year. Coaching When it comes to the offensive coaching staff, they need to focus on fixing the run game. It was semi working during the Ravens game, but this feels more like a one off than fixing it at this stage. It will be interesting to see if they can do anything over the next few weeks, but after the bye week could be the most telling spell. Conclusion Considering the starting shopping list for the offensive side of the ball currently sits at drafting a quarterback, a free agency running back and adding a tight end that can block, it isn't too extreme. Hitting on the quarterback will always be incredibly hard as teams have proven they haven't found a decent way to judge which college quarterbacks will and won't be successful. If they can fix this run game it could be a top offense in the league if they can make the right selection. It is why coming into this season I was incredibly high on the Browns in 2027 and I see no reason to pause the optimism.

item.title: ‘Wasn’t a top pick’-Super Bowl champion explains why Shedeur Sanders has struggled at Browns
item.description: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images Three-time Super Bowl champion Willie McGinest has explained why Shedeur Sanders has struggled to establish himself as the Cleveland Browns’ starting quarterback, arguing that the young signal-caller did not arrive in the NFL with the same pressure as a top draft pick. Sanders has spent much of the current season watching from the sidelines as Deshaun Watson leads Cleveland under head coach Todd Monken. The Browns have made a strong start with Watson at the helm, leaving Sanders facing questions about his future and growing speculation over a potential trade. Willie McGinest says Shedeur Sanders must prove himself on the field McGinest believes Sanders’ draft position played a role in the expectations placed on him when he entered the league. Speaking about the Browns quarterback, the former New England Patriots linebacker said: “Shedeur didn’t put the pressure on the position by coming into the league. I mean that by saying he wasn’t like a top pick. Now, if you’re a number one pick, if you’re a top 10 pick, then you put the pressure on the position right away.” McGinest pointed to Russell Wilson as an example of a later-round pick who quickly forced his way into the starting conversation with the Seattle Seahawks. He argued that Sanders had not yet produced the same evidence to convince Cleveland that he deserved the job. “I know there’s a lot of hype and it’s the hype behind the name or the lineage where you come from or what you are actually doing on the football field. At some point, if he’s doing what he needs to do on the football field, he’ll get an opportunity,” McGinest added. Sanders did start eight games for Cleveland last season after Dillon Gabriel suffered a concussion, throwing seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. His tendency to hold the ball for too long was also a concern, with his average time to throw reaching 3.24 seconds from his debut in Week 11, the highest figure in the NFL over that period. Watson has since strengthened his position as Cleveland’s starter, helping the Browns build a 4-2 record across their first six games. Sanders has also signed with Young Money APAA Sports for representation, a move that has fuelled speculation about his future. However, The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones suggested a trade before the deadline would still be a surprise. Sanders now needs to make the most of his opportunities if he is to change the Browns’ thinking about his role. NFL sends blunt message to Mike Vrabel with hefty fine over officials incident

item.title: Maradona’s Doctor Was Made ‘Scapegoat’ For His Death, Lawyer Tells Court
item.description: A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments Wednesday that his client was innocent and had been made a “scapegoat.” Attorney Roberto Rallin rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s November 2020 death was foreseeable, while another defense attorney, Francisco Oneto, maintained that his death resulted from an “acute and unpredictable” heart attack. “There was absolutely no possibility of predicting this fatal outcome,” Oneto insisted. Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Luque, a neurosurgeon considered a key decision-maker for Maradona at the time of his death. “We are here to proclaim Luque’s innocence, not with television slogans, but with the evidence that supports it,” Rallin said. “Leopoldo Luque has been the scapegoat.” Maradona died at age 60 from a cardiorespiratory crisis coupled with pulmonary edema. He was found dead in his bed at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following surgery for a subdural hematoma. The death of Argentina’s favorite son plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. Tens of thousands of people defied social distancing rules to bid farewell to him as he lay in state at the presidential palace. A total of seven health-care professionals have been on trial since April for potential negligence leading to the star’s death during his two weeks of convalescence. Prosecutors have requested sentences ranging from four to 12 years for six of the seven defendants. In its closing arguments, the prosecution condemned Luque’s “inaction,” saying his attitude “was always to do nothing” in the face of the warning signs that Maradona was exhibiting. Fernando Burlando, lawyer for Gianinna Maradona and Dalma Maradona, daughters of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, arrives at the San Isidro courthouse for the final hearing of defense closing arguments in the trial over the death of Diego Maradona, in San Isidro, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Luis ROBAYO / AFP) | Luis ROBAYO / AFP Contested Medical History Luque’s lawyers particularly attacked the conclusions of the interdisciplinary medical commission, which had been established by the court in 2021 to provide an opinion on the star’s death. The commission, which based its findings on the autopsy and other things, said Maradona had a history of heart problems that should have been taken into account, a conclusion the prosecution emphasized. But Luque’s defense lawyers said that clinical tests done prior to Maradona’s surgery just before his death didn’t reveal any heart issues. “It’s so clear that Maradona didn’t have any heart problems in 2020,” Oneto said during closing arguments. item.content:encoded: A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments Wednesday that his client was innocent and had been made a “scapegoat.” Attorney Roberto Rallin rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s November 2020 death was foreseeable, while another defense attorney, Francisco Oneto, maintained that his death resulted from an “acute and unpredictable” heart attack. “There was absolutely no possibility of predicting this fatal outcome,” Oneto insisted. Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Luque, a neurosurgeon considered a key decision-maker for Maradona at the time of his death. “We are here to proclaim Luque’s innocence, not with television slogans, but with the evidence that supports it,” Rallin said. “Leopoldo Luque has been the scapegoat.” Maradona died at age 60 from a cardiorespiratory crisis coupled with pulmonary edema. He was found dead in his bed at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following surgery for a subdural hematoma. The death of Argentina’s favorite son plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. Tens of thousands of people defied social distancing rules to bid farewell to him as he lay in state at the presidential palace. A total of seven health-care professionals have been on trial since April for potential negligence leading to the star’s death during his two weeks of convalescence. Prosecutors have requested sentences ranging from four to 12 years for six of the seven defendants. In its closing arguments, the prosecution condemned Luque’s “inaction,” saying his attitude “was always to do nothing” in the face of the warning signs that Maradona was exhibiting. Fernando Burlando, lawyer for Gianinna Maradona and Dalma Maradona, daughters of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, arrives at the San Isidro courthouse for the final hearing of defense closing arguments in the trial over the death of Diego Maradona, in San Isidro, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Luis ROBAYO / AFP) | Luis ROBAYO / AFP Contested Medical History Luque’s lawyers particularly attacked the conclusions of the interdisciplinary medical commission, which had been established by the court in 2021 to provide an opinion on the star’s death. The commission, which based its findings on the autopsy and other things, said Maradona had a history of heart problems that should have been taken into account, a conclusion the prosecution emphasized. But Luque’s defense lawyers said that clinical tests done prior to Maradona’s surgery just before his death didn’t reveal any heart issues. “It’s so clear that Maradona didn’t have any heart problems in 2020,” Oneto said during closing arguments. Throughout the trial, Luque was by far the most combative defendant, speaking several times when he felt he was being implicated. His legal team played audio recordings, presented scientific articles and even a video of Maradona’s autopsy, provoking the anger of the footballer’s daughters. “It’s easy to attack me because I’m the one who had the most contact with Maradona,” Luque said in court, asserting that “the only one who would defend me would be Diego.” “I cared deeply for him, I loved him, he was my idol and my friend,” he said. Defense attorney Nicolas D’Albora, who represents medical coordinator Nancy Forlini, also blamed Maradona’s demise on Luque and another doctor, saying they “were obliged to guarantee the patient’s health.” Forlini faces a 10-year sentence for homicide with eventual intent, for an alleged failure to provide basic medical equipment for home care. The defense’s closing arguments are expected to continue until Thursday. AFP The post Maradona’s Doctor Was Made ‘Scapegoat’ For His Death, Lawyer Tells Court appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic welcomes Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg to NBA: ‘Talking crazy’
item.description: There’s a common idiom that most NBA players follow when it comes to the league’s best players: Don’t poke the bear. But when it came to Luka Doncic on Wednesday night during the Lakers’ season-opening blowout win over the Warriors at Crypto.com Arena, Yaxel Lendeborg not only poked the bear , but ignited a barrage of chirping late in the second quarter. And the Slovenian superstar made it clear that whatever the Warriors rookie said was out of bounds. Yaxel Lendeborg defends Luka Doncic during the Lakers’ 127-105 season-opening win over the Warriors on Oct. 21, 2026 in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images “He was talking crazy,” Doncic said. The trash talk started when the Lakers 6-foot-8 guard picked up a shooting foul against Lendeborg late in the second, with Doncic laughing as the No. 11 pick in June’s NBA draft became frustrated with the call. Luka Doncic drives past Yaxel Lendeborg during the first half of the Lakers’ season-opening blowout victory over the Warriors. Getty Images Even after Lendeborg subbed out, Doncic kept talking to the 6-foot-9 forward out of Michigan while he was on the bench after knocking down a fadeaway against Will Richard, and once again while Sandro Mamukelashvili was shooting free throws. Lendeborg picked up a technical foul with 22 seconds left in the first half after he and Doncic, presumably, kept chirping at each other. The punctuation mark to the jawing came right before halftime, when Doncic nailed a buzzer-beating halfcourt shot to give the Lakers a 66-52 lead going into the game’s break. "He was talking crazy" – Luka Doncic on the chirping with Yaxel Lendeborg. Says he's trying not to pick up as many technical fouls and refrained from picking one up tonight. https://t.co/sYqydObQt7 pic.twitter.com/1azX8moQAx — Khobi Price (@khobi_price) October 22, 2026 “Nobody understands what he says,” Austin Reaves quipped of Doncic. “He’s not speaking English. I didn’t understand anything and barely knew anything was going on. So, I know we need an article to come out and I’m going to start paying people to talk s— to him so gets [into] another gear when people start trying to talk to him.” The most impressive part of the back-and-forth was Doncic not picking up a technical foul during the whole ordeal after being assessed 16 technical fouls last season. Luka Doncic and Yaxel Lendeborg look on during a break in the action in the Lakers’ season-opening blowout win over the Warriors. NBAE via Getty Images “I wasn’t trying to talk back this season,” Doncic said. “I’m trying to not get techs. So it was the first time that [it] was not a double tech, because I didn’t say nothing. So I’m working on it. But as you see, it worked great.”

item.title: New Mexico State leans on James Jones, defense to outlast Sam Houston, 30-24
item.description: New Mexico State celebrates after 30-24 win over Sam Houston on October 22, 2026 | Steve Helwick Sam Houston had a chance to defend its home turf in a standalone Wednesday night Weekday CUSA matchup. Instead, New Mexico State left Huntsville with a long-awaited breakthrough. Behind a career-best performance from running back James Jones and a suffocating defensive effort, the Aggies defeated the Bearkats 30-24 at Bowers Stadium, securing their first road victory of the 2026 season. “We did a good job coming out and getting the first victory of the season,” New Mexico State head coach Tony Sanchez said. “I thought our guys played a good game, played a good four-quarter game, and it was really good to see at the end, with four minutes left, them kicking the ball deep and us being able to just run the clock out. Proud of our guys and happy for them.” The star of the night was Jones, who continued to lead the CUSA in rushing. The New Mexico State running back recorded his fourth 100-yard game of 2026 and shattered his career-high with 178 yards. He also opened the Aggies’ scoring in the second quarter with his lone touchdown of the night. “It’s a blessing,” Jones said of his performance. “I thank the Lord for every opportunity that He gave me. I appreciate what He’s given me. And my o-line, I can’t do it without them. Them up front fighting, our defense getting stops, we’re all playing together. It isn’t even on me, it’s up front.” Jones saved his best work for the final minutes. Clinging to a 6-point lead, New Mexico State leaned on its star running back to drain the final 4:00 of clock and deny the Bearkats an opportunity at a comeback victory. Jones gained 39 yards on four carries during the final drive, converting a 4th-and-2 with 29 seconds remaining to seal the Aggies’ first one-score victory since November 2025. “The final four minutes, I told my coach — Coach (David) Yost does a great job calling plays — but I was telling him, ‘I need the ball in my hands. I’m gonna ice it,’” Jones said. “Then the o-line was doing their thing up front, and then I popped one. That’s what got us in that situation — the o-line up front.” Despite the victory, New Mexico State’s offense had to overcome a pair of costly mistakes early in the game. Roughly two minutes into the contest, the Aggies fell behind 7-0 when Sam Houston wide receiver Terrence Guillory II blocked a punt and Railyn Adams recovered the loose ball in the end zone. Then in the second quarter, New Mexico State’s incomplete lateral pass in its own territory was ruled a fumble, and the Bearkats cashed in with a field goal. item.content:encoded: New Mexico State celebrates after 30-24 win over Sam Houston on October 22, 2026 | Steve Helwick Sam Houston had a chance to defend its home turf in a standalone Wednesday night Weekday CUSA matchup. Instead, New Mexico State left Huntsville with a long-awaited breakthrough. Behind a career-best performance from running back James Jones and a suffocating defensive effort, the Aggies defeated the Bearkats 30-24 at Bowers Stadium, securing their first road victory of the 2026 season. “We did a good job coming out and getting the first victory of the season,” New Mexico State head coach Tony Sanchez said. “I thought our guys played a good game, played a good four-quarter game, and it was really good to see at the end, with four minutes left, them kicking the ball deep and us being able to just run the clock out. Proud of our guys and happy for them.” The star of the night was Jones, who continued to lead the CUSA in rushing. The New Mexico State running back recorded his fourth 100-yard game of 2026 and shattered his career-high with 178 yards. He also opened the Aggies’ scoring in the second quarter with his lone touchdown of the night. “It’s a blessing,” Jones said of his performance. “I thank the Lord for every opportunity that He gave me. I appreciate what He’s given me. And my o-line, I can’t do it without them. Them up front fighting, our defense getting stops, we’re all playing together. It isn’t even on me, it’s up front.” Jones saved his best work for the final minutes. Clinging to a 6-point lead, New Mexico State leaned on its star running back to drain the final 4:00 of clock and deny the Bearkats an opportunity at a comeback victory. Jones gained 39 yards on four carries during the final drive, converting a 4th-and-2 with 29 seconds remaining to seal the Aggies’ first one-score victory since November 2025. “The final four minutes, I told my coach — Coach (David) Yost does a great job calling plays — but I was telling him, ‘I need the ball in my hands. I’m gonna ice it,’” Jones said. “Then the o-line was doing their thing up front, and then I popped one. That’s what got us in that situation — the o-line up front.” Despite the victory, New Mexico State’s offense had to overcome a pair of costly mistakes early in the game. Roughly two minutes into the contest, the Aggies fell behind 7-0 when Sam Houston wide receiver Terrence Guillory II blocked a punt and Railyn Adams recovered the loose ball in the end zone. Then in the second quarter, New Mexico State’s incomplete lateral pass in its own territory was ruled a fumble, and the Bearkats cashed in with a field goal. New Mexico State’s defense ensured those miscues did not prove costly. The Aggies allowed just 13 yards in the first half, surrendering 20 in the opening quarter before holding Sam Houston to -7 yards in the second. The Bearkats finished with just nine first downs and 11 rushing yards, repeatedly struggling to win at the line of scrimmage. “I thought our defense played lights out,” Sanchez said. “Other than that very first snap of the second half, the guys did a fantastic job of creating pressure on the quarterback all night. We got some important turnovers and they did a really good job.” Sanchez also credited his offense for its response, and New Mexico State captured its first lead in the final seconds of the first half on a 2-play, 43-yard touchdown drive that consumed just 18 seconds. “Offensively, it was really good to see us put that touchdown on the board before halftime and come out early in the second half and get another touchdown,” Sanchez said. The Aggies’ defense came up with two crucial turnovers, each setting up a short field that led to a touchdown. In the second quarter, Josiah Charles intercepted Sam Houston quarterback Landyn Locke and returned the ball to the 1-yard line, setting up Jones’ touchdown. Late in the third quarter, Kaian Roberts-Day blew up a flea-flicker in the backfield and recovered the fumble, setting up TJ Washington Jr. for a rushing touchdown. “We’ve lost the turnover battle three weeks in a row,” said Sanchez, whose team was a minus-5 in turnover margin prior to Wednesday. “It’s really gotten in the way. You go all the way back to the Hawaii game, obviously the UNM game, the FIU game, and we weren’t winning the turnover battle. We had one really bad turnover at the end, but to win the turnover battle tonight made a big difference in the game.” Sam Houston’s offense finally found the explosive play it desperately needed to open the second half. After leaving the game in the second quarter with a leg injury, Locke returned to action and connected with Tim Burns Jr. for an 81-yard touchdown on the first snap after halftime, handing the Bearkats a 17-14 lead. Locke’s longest pass since Week 2 ended the team’s 12-quarter drought without an offensive touchdown, dating back to Sept. 26. Locke was briefly replaced by true freshman backup Brett Holloway before finishing the game with 235 passing yards. Sam Houston head coach Phil Longo explained the injury situation postgame. “They thought it was a fibula fracture, and they X-ray’d him, and you’re looking at losing your starting quarterback for the year,” Longo said. “Then 20 minutes goes by and no fracture, and they tape him up, we’re gonna treat him, and he comes back out and he couldn’t really move laterally, so we held him out for a little bit. We ran him around the sideline to see if he could move enough to do the things he needs to do. When he proved to me that he could do that and the trainers gave me the okay, we put him back on the field. For playing hurt, he actually played fairly decent in the second half.” The Bearkats’ momentum after Locke’s touchdown pass was brief. New Mexico State responded three minutes later with a touchdown strike from Adam Damante to AJ Williams III. The touchdown sparked a 16-0 run that put the Aggies back in control. It wasn’t Williams’ only highlight Wednesday night. The 6’4” wide receiver had an additional contested catch in the end zone, finishing the night with two touchdowns — both which handed New Mexico State the lead. “AJ has been waiting on this,” Jones said. “I’m very happy for him that everybody got to see what he can do, because he’s been doing it in practice all year.” Sam Houston eventually responded cutting the deficit to 30-24 with an MJ Dowdy rushing touchdown with four minutes remaining. But the Bearkats could not regain possession, as Jones and the Aggies’ offensive line dominated the final series. “I thought we challenged them from a heart and emotional and a grind standpoint in the second half, and they responded,” Longo said. “But too little, too late, obviously, so that’s kinda how the game went. We responded, played more physical, played with some more emotion and some passion offensively in the second half but came up short because it wasn’t enough.” Longo also commented on Sam Houston’s recurring offensive struggles in a night they were outgained by the visitor 203-11 on the ground. “I didn’t see yardage, that’s for sure,” Longo said on the offensive performance. “We addressed a lot of the issues we’d had the past two weeks. I think a lot of people understand we’re struggling up front because of some injuries. You gotta plug in the next guy and you gotta go. We even tried to redirect our plan this week, just to try and play maybe to the strengths of some of the guys we have in. But we just lack continuity up front right now, and it’s affecting us offensively.” Sam Houston (1-6, 0-3 CUSA) remains winless against FBS competition this season and has fallen to 3-16 in the Longo era. The Bearkats are on the brink of missing bowl eligibility for the second consecutive season, and to preserve those hopes, they must respond on the road Tuesday at Missouri State. “There’s a sense of urgency from the get-go,” Longo said. “I want for us to manage some of the issues we’re having on offense and fix them. item.title: Russian strikes kill 7 in Ukraine after US envoy meets Putin
item.description: Russia and Ukraine traded attacks overnight, with seven killed on the Ukrainian side, authorities said on Thursday, shortly after US President Donald Trump’s envoy held talks with Russian leader Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg. Trump sought to strike an optimistic tone after US envoy Steve Witkoff’s meeting with Putin on Wednesday, saying negotiators were “maybe now the closest we’ve been” to ending the war. The Kremlin indicated it was “in principle” open to the resumption of trilateral talks involving the two sides and the United States. But attacks did not let up in the wake of the visit. Moscow’s mayor Sergei Sobyanin said two people had been wounded in huge barrages of 630 drones fired towards the region, 163 of which were approaching the Russian capital. The governor of nearby Tula region said Russian air defences had destroyed 70 drones. Another man was wounded in the Lipetsk region, its governor said. In Ukraine, the attacks killed one man in Sumy and a woman in Kharkiv, both in the northeast, as well as three people in southeastern Zaporizhzhia and two in the eastern region of Donetsk, authorities said. Kyiv’s mayor Vitali Klitschko said on social media strikes had wounded 15 people in the Ukrainian capital. He said the strikes had damaged metro infrastructure at the Pivdenny Bridge, which officials said had restricted traffic between parts of the city. Ukraine’s air force posted a warning in the early hours of “more ballistic missiles towards Kyiv” and instructed residents to stay in shelters. Witkoff had flown to Russia from a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo on Tuesday, which was aimed at smoothing over a bitter rift between Trump and the Ukrainian leader. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also took part in the talks with Putin remotely. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that Russia was “in principle, ready to resume” trilateral talks in mid-November — after the US midterm elections — and that the Kremlin wanted them to focus on post-war security. Zelensky said Ukraine also backed resuming trilateral talks. – ‘Work left to do’ – Ushakov said Witkoff briefed Putin on “some new aspects in the approaches of the Europeans and Kyiv” from the Oslo meeting, but that “there wasn’t really much substance in them”. A summit between Putin, Trump and China’s Xi Jinping was also being prepared in China’s Shenzhen for next month, Ushakov said, calling it “the first such meeting in history”. During their three-hour meeting, Witkoff praised Putin for granting Trump’s request to free US citizen Stephen Hubbard, a retired English teacher in his 70s who had been detained for fighting for Ukraine — charges he denied. “You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian — you are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,” Witkoff said. item.content:encoded: Russia and Ukraine traded attacks overnight, with seven killed on the Ukrainian side, authorities said on Thursday, shortly after US President Donald Trump’s envoy held talks with Russian leader Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg. Trump sought to strike an optimistic tone after US envoy Steve Witkoff’s meeting with Putin on Wednesday, saying negotiators were “maybe now the closest we’ve been” to ending the war. The Kremlin indicated it was “in principle” open to the resumption of trilateral talks involving the two sides and the United States. But attacks did not let up in the wake of the visit. Moscow’s mayor Sergei Sobyanin said two people had been wounded in huge barrages of 630 drones fired towards the region, 163 of which were approaching the Russian capital. The governor of nearby Tula region said Russian air defences had destroyed 70 drones. Another man was wounded in the Lipetsk region, its governor said. In Ukraine, the attacks killed one man in Sumy and a woman in Kharkiv, both in the northeast, as well as three people in southeastern Zaporizhzhia and two in the eastern region of Donetsk, authorities said. Kyiv’s mayor Vitali Klitschko said on social media strikes had wounded 15 people in the Ukrainian capital. He said the strikes had damaged metro infrastructure at the Pivdenny Bridge, which officials said had restricted traffic between parts of the city. Ukraine’s air force posted a warning in the early hours of “more ballistic missiles towards Kyiv” and instructed residents to stay in shelters. Witkoff had flown to Russia from a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo on Tuesday, which was aimed at smoothing over a bitter rift between Trump and the Ukrainian leader. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also took part in the talks with Putin remotely. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that Russia was “in principle, ready to resume” trilateral talks in mid-November — after the US midterm elections — and that the Kremlin wanted them to focus on post-war security. Zelensky said Ukraine also backed resuming trilateral talks. – ‘Work left to do’ – Ushakov said Witkoff briefed Putin on “some new aspects in the approaches of the Europeans and Kyiv” from the Oslo meeting, but that “there wasn’t really much substance in them”. A summit between Putin, Trump and China’s Xi Jinping was also being prepared in China’s Shenzhen for next month, Ushakov said, calling it “the first such meeting in history”. During their three-hour meeting, Witkoff praised Putin for granting Trump’s request to free US citizen Stephen Hubbard, a retired English teacher in his 70s who had been detained for fighting for Ukraine — charges he denied. “You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian — you are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,” Witkoff said. Witkoff said on social media the talks with Putin were “constructive” but that “there is still important work left to do”. Discussions would continue between the United States, Ukraine and Russia at the technical level, he added. Trump returned to power in January 2025 promising to end the war in 24 hours — but more than a year of US-led talks have failed to produce a breakthrough. In recent days, a frustrated Trump has once again pivoted away from Ukraine and back to Putin, trumpeting what he said was a deal for Russia to sell diesel and reduce prices sent soaring by his Iran war. Trump also delayed the imposition of sanctions on Russia’s war machine — a decision he defended on Wednesday as necessary to secure Hubbard’s release. “If you would’ve put those sanctions on… you could forget about him. You’d never see him again,” Trump told reporters at the White House. Witkoff told Putin Washington was “grateful” for the diesel deal, which sparked outrage in Kyiv and across Europe. The war, Europe’s worst since World War II, has killed tens of thousands of people since Russia’s February 2022 invasion. Putin has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Zelensky and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine. item.title: Steve Kerr Gives Terrible Warriors Update For Stephen Curry Fans
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr speaks to Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors during the first half of their preseason game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on October 06, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty One of the biggest topics about the Golden State Warriors this season is about whether they’d make a big trade. More help is needed for Stephen Curry to have any chance of contending for another NBA Championship with this Warriors core. Jimmy Butler will miss the start of the season with his injury recovery to see minimal help behind Curry on the flawed roster. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr shut down any chance of Golden State risking their future to help Curry: “Do we throw away our entire future to build around a 39-year-old Steph? He turns 39 in March, right? Does it make sense now to throw away all those picks? Hell no,. Our fan base might have been thrilled if we had traded five firsts and two of our better players for one of the big fish. They might have been happy for a year, and they might have been miserable for the next decade if it backfired.” Kerr’s blunt comment upsets Curry fans who believe the Warriors owe it to him to add more star power. Curry helped lead the Warriors to relevance after years of struggles before his arrival. Most Golden State fans hold immense loyalty to Curry, Draymond Green, and Klay Thompson for changing the culture. Will The Warriors Make Any Moves To Help Stephen Curry? The situation in Golden State is dire with a terrible opening night performances against the Los Angeles Lakers . It is hard to see this roster competing for a playoff spot in the loaded Western Conference with talented teams trying to make the play-in. Curry needs help with the news of Kristaps Porzingis being ruled out indefinitely with an unknown illness. The Warriors kept most of the same roster from last season to see the same issues returning and frustrating the fan base. Anthony Davis and Trey Murphy are the most common names linked to Golden State. Unfortunately, Kerr’s comment about not trading future picks or young prospects likely blocks both moves. Opposing teams want real talent, and the Warriors are not looking to give up anything of value to increase their chances of winning now. Could Stephen Curry Want To Leave Warriors? The next question for such a quote focuses on what Curry feels about it. Most quotes from Curry confirms he wants to retire with the Warriors as a rare one franchise superstar. However, the lack of moves could mean he’s retiring in irrelevance if they don’t change course. The situation in Golden State is dire with a terrible opening night performances against the Los Angeles Lakers . It is hard to see this roster competing for a playoff spot in the loaded Western Conference with talented teams trying to make the play-in. Curry needs help with the news of Kristaps Porzingis being ruled out indefinitely with an unknown illness. The Warriors kept most of the same roster from last season to see the same issues returning and frustrating the fan base. Anthony Davis and Trey Murphy are the most common names linked to Golden State. Unfortunately, Kerr’s comment about not trading future picks or young prospects likely blocks both moves. Opposing teams want real talent, and the Warriors are not looking to give up anything of value to increase their chances of winning now. Could Stephen Curry Want To Leave Warriors? The next question for such a quote focuses on what Curry feels about it. Most quotes from Curry confirms he wants to retire with the Warriors as a rare one franchise superstar. However, the lack of moves could mean he’s retiring in irrelevance if they don’t change course. Next season will see Golden State holding a lot of cap space with Green and Butler entering free agency. It appears the Warriors would rather pay a free agent rather than trade assets to get better faster. The Washington Wizards could let Davis walk if he wants too much money. Curry could opt to force his way out via a trade demand, but the odds are against that. Even in a losing scenario, Curry’s reputation and legacy matter more in Golden State than on a new contender. item.title: The Wayward Train: My Dad’s Notre Dame Thanksgiving Adventure in 1963
item.description: An unforgettable Thanksgiving, a football game at Yankee Stadium, and a train ride that took an unexpected detour through Canada. Since Notre Dame has a bye week, I thought we’d take this week’s Throwback Thursday a little off the rails. Literally. Instead of revisiting a memorable victory or one of those classic Notre Dame football games that still makes us smile, I’m sharing a story from my dad’s college days. It’s a story that involves Thanksgiving on Long Island, a football game at Yankee Stadium, one of the most difficult moments in American history, and a train ride home that turned into an international adventure. Oh, and there’s a photograph of my dad sleeping upside down in his train seat. Yes, you read that correctly. But before we get to the train, we need to go back to Thanksgiving 1963. A Thanksgiving Invitation My dad was a student at Notre Dame when his classmate Mike Fiore invited him and a few friends to spend Thanksgiving with his family on Long Island. The plan was to enjoy the holiday with Mike’s family, explore a little of New York, and attend Notre Dame’s Thanksgiving Day football game against Syracuse at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx. Mike was studying civil engineering at Notre Dame, following in the footsteps of his father, who was also a Notre Dame graduate. My dad remembers Mike’s father as a highly accomplished civil engineer who had worked on bridge projects. The Fiore family welcomed the young men into their home for the Thanksgiving holiday, treating them to a wonderful dinner and giving them the opportunity to explore Long Island and New York City during their visit. They arrived Wednesday evening, attended the Notre Dame–Syracuse game at Yankee Stadium on Thanksgiving morning, and spent the rest of the holiday weekend enjoying time with friends before heading back to South Bend on Sunday. For a group of college students, it sounded like a pretty terrific Thanksgiving getaway. But the timing made this particular holiday unlike any other. On November 22, 1963, just six days before Notre Dame and Syracuse would meet at Yankee Stadium, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas. When I asked my dad what he remembered about that Thanksgiving, he told me the country was still very much in shock. It’s difficult to imagine what those days must have felt like for a group of young college students. They were away from campus, spending time with friends, and looking forward to a football game, but the entire nation was grieving. item.content:encoded: An unforgettable Thanksgiving, a football game at Yankee Stadium, and a train ride that took an unexpected detour through Canada. Since Notre Dame has a bye week, I thought we’d take this week’s Throwback Thursday a little off the rails. Literally. Instead of revisiting a memorable victory or one of those classic Notre Dame football games that still makes us smile, I’m sharing a story from my dad’s college days. It’s a story that involves Thanksgiving on Long Island, a football game at Yankee Stadium, one of the most difficult moments in American history, and a train ride home that turned into an international adventure. Oh, and there’s a photograph of my dad sleeping upside down in his train seat. Yes, you read that correctly. But before we get to the train, we need to go back to Thanksgiving 1963. A Thanksgiving Invitation My dad was a student at Notre Dame when his classmate Mike Fiore invited him and a few friends to spend Thanksgiving with his family on Long Island. The plan was to enjoy the holiday with Mike’s family, explore a little of New York, and attend Notre Dame’s Thanksgiving Day football game against Syracuse at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx. Mike was studying civil engineering at Notre Dame, following in the footsteps of his father, who was also a Notre Dame graduate. My dad remembers Mike’s father as a highly accomplished civil engineer who had worked on bridge projects. The Fiore family welcomed the young men into their home for the Thanksgiving holiday, treating them to a wonderful dinner and giving them the opportunity to explore Long Island and New York City during their visit. They arrived Wednesday evening, attended the Notre Dame–Syracuse game at Yankee Stadium on Thanksgiving morning, and spent the rest of the holiday weekend enjoying time with friends before heading back to South Bend on Sunday. For a group of college students, it sounded like a pretty terrific Thanksgiving getaway. But the timing made this particular holiday unlike any other. On November 22, 1963, just six days before Notre Dame and Syracuse would meet at Yankee Stadium, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas. When I asked my dad what he remembered about that Thanksgiving, he told me the country was still very much in shock. It’s difficult to imagine what those days must have felt like for a group of young college students. They were away from campus, spending time with friends, and looking forward to a football game, but the entire nation was grieving. And Notre Dame’s football team had experienced that historic week in a particularly unusual way. A Football Season Overshadowed by History In 2018, Notre Dame published a fascinating retrospective titled “Yankee Stadium, Circa 1963,” written by Matt Storin, who had served as the senior manager of the 1963 Fighting Irish football team. Storin, a member of Notre Dame’s Class of 1964 who went on to a distinguished journalism career, offered a firsthand look at a difficult season and an unforgettable Thanksgiving week. Notre Dame had been scheduled to face Iowa on November 23, the day after Kennedy’s assassination. According to Storin, the Irish had already arrived in Iowa City and settled into their hotel when the game was canceled. The team returned to South Bend on Sunday morning, only to turn around and travel to New York on Wednesday for its Thanksgiving matchup with Syracuse. The Irish were struggling through a season in which victories had been hard to come by. Under interim head coach Hugh Devore, Notre Dame had won just two of its first eight games. There was also uncertainty beyond the football field. Storin recalled the economic anxiety surrounding South Bend as Studebaker announced plans to end automobile production in the city. Between the assassination, the struggling football program, and concerns about the local economy, it was a particularly difficult time for the Notre Dame community. Yet the football season continued. Storin remembered the team arriving in New York and checking into the Waldorf Astoria. The traveling squad numbered fewer than 40 players, and the players had little time to prepare once they reached the city. The Thanksgiving Day game would kick off at 10:30 in the morning, an unusual start time by today’s standards, before a crowd of 56,672 at the original Yankee Stadium. For Storin, walking through the third-base dugout and onto the famous playing field was an unforgettable experience. For my dad and his friends, it was another chance to cheer on the Irish. Unfortunately, the game itself would provide yet another frustrating chapter in Notre Dame’s 1963 season. Notre Dame vs. Syracuse: A Familiar Ending The 1963 Notre Dame Football Review described Yankee Stadium as an unusual setting for college football. The enormous grandstands towered above the players, casting long shadows across the field and blocking much of the late-November sunlight. The Irish had experienced several heartbreaking losses that season, and the Syracuse game would follow a painfully familiar pattern. Syracuse controlled much of the early action but repeatedly failed to capitalize on scoring opportunities. On one promising drive, Orange running back Jim Nance fumbled near the Notre Dame goal line, and Tom Longo recovered for the Irish. Eventually, Syracuse broke through when Wally Mahle connected with Billy Hunter on a six-yard touchdown pass. Dick Arrington blocked the extra-point attempt, leaving Notre Dame trailing 6-0. Late in the second quarter, the Irish finally found some offensive momentum. Starting at their own 14-yard line, Notre Dame put together an impressive 86-yard scoring drive. Nick Rassas gained 20 yards around right end, Jim Kelly hauled in a 15-yard pass from Sandy Bonvechio, and Tommy MacDonald helped move the Irish deep into Syracuse territory. Then Notre Dame reached into its bag of tricks. Bonvechio pitched the ball to halfback Frank Budka, who threw a touchdown pass to MacDonald in the end zone. Ken Ivan added the extra point, giving Notre Dame a 7-6 lead with just one minute remaining in the first half. For a team that had struggled so much throughout the season, perhaps this would finally be the afternoon when everything came together. The Irish defense certainly did its part. Bill Pfeiffer intercepted a Syracuse pass in the third quarter, and MacDonald added another interception to his impressive career total. Bob Lehmann and Ken Maglicic also helped thwart Syracuse scoring opportunities as the Irish clung to their narrow lead. But the fourth quarter brought another heartbreaking finish. With 3:28 remaining, Syracuse quarterback Rich King connected with Mike Koski for the go-ahead touchdown. A successful two-point conversion extended the Orange lead to 14-7. Notre Dame couldn’t answer, and the Irish fell to Syracuse by seven points. In his 2018 recollection, Storin described the loss as the fourth time that season Notre Dame had surrendered a game-deciding score late in the contest. He also remembered an exchange with a Syracuse player after the game. The player sympathized with Notre Dame’s difficult afternoon, and Storin replied that it had been much like the rest of the season. Sometimes, that’s just the way football goes. One interesting detail from Storin’s account is that Notre Dame wore green jerseys that Thanksgiving Day. The Irish wouldn’t wear green again until the famous 1977 game against USC. And although nobody knew it at the time, the 1963 season was about to become an important turning point in Notre Dame football history. Just 18 days after the Syracuse game, Notre Dame announced that Northwestern head coach Ara Parseghian would take over the program. The Irish would go from a 2-7 season in 1963 to a 9-1 record in 1964, narrowly missing a national championship. But back on Thanksgiving weekend in 1963, none of that was known. My dad and his friends had enjoyed a holiday with the Fiore family, watched

item.title: The Netherlands returns looted Benin artefact, 129 years after
item.description: …Oba Ewuare II to reestablish ties with Portugal By Ozioruva Aliu The Netherlands, Tuesday, returned a Benin artefact to the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, 129 years after the invasion of the Benin Kingdom. The presentation took place at the Oba’s Palace in Benin City as part of activities marking the traditional ruler’s 10th coronation anniversary. Meanwhile, as part of activities marking his 10th year coronation anniversary, the Oba of Benin has promised to re-establish ties with Portugal, which was the first European country to come into the kingdom. Chairman of the 10th Coronation Anniversary Committee and former Deputy Governor of Edo State, Chief Lucky Imasue, said The Netherlands had initiated the return of artefacts taken from Benin following the 1897 invasion. Imasue said every Benin artefact belonged to the Oba of Benin, regardless of the quantity, adding that more artefacts were expected to be returned. He said the artefact was presented by the Consul General of the Netherlands, Mr. Frank Keurnorst, alongside Beatrice van Bormann, Executive Director of Museum De Fundatie, in the Netherlands. He described the return on October 20, as significant, coming exactly 10 years after Ewuare’s coronation and 129 years after many historical objects were looted from the Benin Kingdom. Imasue recalled that the artefacts documented the majesty of the Oba and life in the kingdom, describing them as historical records kept in the palace before the invasion. “Efforts to recover the artefacts date back to previous Obas, but gained momentum under Ewuare, whose diplomatic experience as a former ambassador helped advance the campaign,” he said. According to him, the Federal Government, through the National Commission for Museums and Monuments, recognises that the artefacts were taken from the Oba’s palace and should be returned there. He thanked the government and people of the Netherlands for returning the artefact and choosing the Oba’s coronation anniversary for the presentation. Oba Ewuare II to reestablish ties with Portugal In his anniversary address, Oba Ewuare II commended Ambassador Santos and the Consul General of Portugal for attending, describing their presence as fortuitous. “We have a very unique link with the Portuguese. When I was told that the Portuguese Ambassador was around, it was like telepathy, because I had been thinking already about Portugal,” Oba Ewuare II said. He recalled that the Holy Aruosa Church in Benin was established during the Portuguese era when his forefathers attempted to adopt the Catholic faith but retained traditional beliefs. He explained that the church’s practices and regalia were modelled along Catholic lines, while the kingdom maintained its traditional spiritual portals of communication with God Almighty. Meanwhile, as part of activities marking his 10th year coronation anniversary, the Oba of Benin has promised to re-establish ties with Portugal, which was the first European country to come into the kingdom. Chairman of the 10th Coronation Anniversary Committee and former Deputy Governor of Edo State, Chief Lucky Imasue, said The Netherlands had initiated the return of artefacts taken from Benin following the 1897 invasion. Imasue said every Benin artefact belonged to the Oba of Benin, regardless of the quantity, adding that more artefacts were expected to be returned. According to him, the Federal Government, through the National Commission for Museums and Monuments, recognises that the artefacts were taken from the Oba’s palace and should be returned there. He thanked the government and people of the Netherlands for returning the artefact and choosing the Oba’s coronation anniversary for the presentation. Oba Ewuare II to reestablish ties with Portugal In his anniversary address, Oba Ewuare II commended Ambassador Santos and the Consul General of Portugal for attending, describing their presence as fortuitous. “We have a very unique link with the Portuguese. When I was told that the Portuguese Ambassador was around, it was like telepathy, because I had been thinking already about Portugal,” Oba Ewuare II said. He recalled that the Holy Aruosa Church in Benin was established during the Portuguese era when his forefathers attempted to adopt the Catholic faith but retained traditional beliefs. He explained that the church’s practices and regalia were modelled along Catholic lines, while the kingdom maintained its traditional spiritual portals of communication with God Almighty. The monarch recalled his experience as Nigeria’s Ambassador in Rome, where he was pleasantly surprised to learn that the Vatican had started recognising African traditional religions. The Oba said one of his sons is an admirer of Portuguese football star, Cristiano Ronaldo, and commended Beatriz for taking an assignment to heart and succeeding. He said his late mother’s (Iyeoba) teachings urging him not to embarrass or bring shame to her, and to pray to God to protect him from worldly temptations contributed to who he is today. item.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
item.description: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.” Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.” Continue reading...

item.title: Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes criticised manager Michael Carrick’s tactics following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como on Wednesday night had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. “Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat,” said Fernandes. “It’s difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. “If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.” Fernandes also highlighted United’s passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Fernandes is the latest United player to publicly break ranks. Defender Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid last week. Martinez said Carrick had been left with an understrength squad. He later apologised. Youri Tielemans, who started alongside Fernandes in the United midfield in Italy, admitted the display was simply not good enough. “We got outplayed for most of the game so it was a very disappointing night,” said Tielemans. “You can be good tactically but if the effort is not good (then it will not work) and vice versa. You need to be good at everything and tonight we were poor.” AFP The post Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

He later apologised. Youri Tielemans, who started alongside Fernandes in the United midfield in Italy, admitted the display was simply not good enough. “We got outplayed for most of the game so it was a very disappointing night,” said Tielemans. “You can be good tactically but if the effort is not good (then it will not work) and vice versa. You need to be good at everything and tonight we were poor.” AFP The post Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Court warns defence against delay in trial of 4 suspects over DSS officer’s murder

Justice Joyce Abdulmalik gave the warning after Kelvin Ekwe and Geoffrey Uwadiegu, who appeared for the defendants, expressed unreadiness to commence trial and sought an application for adjournment. When the case was called, Munirat Oladunjoye, who represented the prosecution, informed the court that the matter was fixed for trial following the defendants’ denial of the allegations. She, however, told the court that the prosecution had an application to shield the identity of their witnesses pursuant to Section 232(3)(b) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA), 2015. Oladunjoye, therefore, prayed the court for an order granting the permission to mask their witnesses and not to reveal their names. But lawyer to the 1st and 2nd defendants, Kelvin Ekwe, disagreed with Oladunjoye’s oral application. He argued that such application was uncalled for. Ekwe submitted that from the proof of evidence served on them, only a witness was listed as DSS investigation officer. According to him, there is no evidence that if the witnesses are not masked, it will prejudice the prosecution’s case. Besides, he argued that the application should be formally filed for them to respond appropriately and to guard against ambush. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: * Adjourns to 28 October The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday warned the defence lawyers against delay in the trial of four suspects who allegedly kidnapped and killed Ekpeyong Asuquo Owoh, an operative of the Department of State Services (DSS). Justice Joyce Abdulmalik gave the warning after Kelvin Ekwe and Geoffrey Uwadiegu, who appeared for the defendants, expressed unreadiness to commence trial and sought an application for adjournment. When the case was called, Munirat Oladunjoye, who represented the prosecution, informed the court that the matter was fixed for trial following the defendants’ denial of the allegations. She, however, told the court that the prosecution had an application to shield the identity of their witnesses pursuant to Section 232(3)(b) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA), 2015. Oladunjoye, therefore, prayed the court for an order granting the permission to mask their witnesses and not to reveal their names. But lawyer to the 1st and 2nd defendants, Kelvin Ekwe, disagreed with Oladunjoye’s oral application. He argued that such application was uncalled for. Ekwe submitted that from the proof of evidence served on them, only a witness was listed as DSS investigation officer. According to him, there is no evidence that if the witnesses are not masked, it will prejudice the prosecution’s case. Besides, he argued that the application should be formally filed for them to respond appropriately and to guard against ambush. Justice Abdulmalik then asked Ekwe to cite any law to back his argument that the prosecution must file a formal application to make such request. Responding, the lawyer said he relied on Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution. Oladunjoye also countered Ekwe’s submission. In a short ruling, the judge agreed with the DSS lawyer’s submission. Justice Abdulmalik held that in the light that the case being a terrorism matter, it would not serve the interest of justice to expose the identity of the witnesses in the case. The judge, who directed the trial to commence and the witness to be co-named as “AB”, ordered that anyone who runs foul of Section 232(5) of ACJA will be liable to one year jail term. Geoffrey Uwadiegwu, counsel to the 3rd and 4th defendants, informed the court that he was coming into the matter for the first and and that he would need more time to study the case file. Ekwe also told the court that he was just served with the video evidence by the prosecution, insisting that he was not ready to go on with the trial. The prosecution lawyer responded that though Ekwe was just being served with the video evidence, the video clip would not be used in today’s trial. She prayed the court to allow the matter to proceed. Oladunjoye argued that Ekwe’s absence on October 6 caused the case to be adjourned. Dissatisfied, Ekwe and Uwadiegwu stood up at the same time to address court on why the matter must be adjourned. But the judge cautioned them against unruly behaviour in her court. “I run my court in line with international best practice, and that is why people say I am strict. “So, when I run my court, there should be 99.9 per cent compliance according to international best practice,” she said. Justice Abdulmalik said she wouldn’t have listed the case for hearing because there were many pre-election cases in the docket of the court. She added that she had at least nine judgments to write in respect of pre-election matters which must be delivered before Nov. 9. The judge, however, said that she saw the case as very crucial and which should be determined expeditiously. Having listened to the parties, Justice Abdulmalik agreed to give a short adjournment. She, however, warned against any act that could delay the trial. The judge consequently adjourned the matter until 28 October at the instance of the two defence lawyers. Suspects The suspects, Michael Okafor, a.k.a Onyechimeleze; Chinedu Chukwudozie, alias Kante; Chibunna Olisa; and Chigozie Olisa, a.k.a Ability were arraigned before Justice Abdulmalik on 28 September on a six-count charge bordering on terrorism and kidnapping. The prosecution alleged that the defendants conspired to commit acts of terrorism and were involved in the abduction of Owoh, while he was travelling from Port Harcourt in Rivers to Awka in Anambra. They were further accused of taking the operative hostage and causing his death in the course of the alleged criminal operation. The suspects were also accused of belonging to the proscribed IPOB and its armed wing, the Eastern Security Network (ESN), as well as involvement in activities allegedly linked to terrorism. In addition, the prosecution alleged that the suspects were involved in the unlawful possession of firearms, including AK-47 and pump-action rifles, in connection with the alleged offences. The charges followed investigations into the circumstances surrounding the abduction and killing of the officer and the alleged activities of the defendants. item.title: Certification authority eMudhra defends its laughably weak private keys
item.description: Indian certification authority eMudhra has defended the laughably weak private keys it used to sign some digital certificates it issued, and suggested others should share the blame for the incident. In case you’re coming to this one late, news broke yesterday that private keys the company used to sign certs were beyond weak: one was literally just the number “4,” and several others were short strings of easily guessed two-or-three-digit numbers. It’s easy to deduce the value of those keys, which makes it possible to forge certs and impersonate websites or other resources. That’s gold for scammers, phishers, and other miscreants. The entire infosec industry has pointed that out, urged swift adoption of better certs, and lamented the fact that implementing replacements will be a long and thankless task. eMudhra’s statement about the incident says it generated keys during “a Key Generation Ceremony (KGC) held on April 30, 2025, using FIPS 140-2 Level 3 Hardware Security Modules (HSMs).” Such hardware is the standard kit for the job and should in theory produce nicely complex keys and store them securely. But something went wrong. “A flaw in the KGC caused a wrap/unwrap step to produce a second set of weak keys alongside the original strong keys,” the statement claims. “The weak keys were the ones published to the browser root stores. eMudhra is working to establish the root cause.” The company then gets a tad defensive. “These roots and issuing CAs have gone through independent audits for two years in a row and have been in browser trust lists since mid-2025,” the statement adds, seemingly shifting some blame to auditors and other stakeholders. The announcement then points out that eMudhra’s TLS business generates just one percent of its revenue, meaning this mess won’t impact its bottom line too much. That’s nice to know for the company’s investors but rather misses the point that whoever relies on the company now has an urgent, unwanted, and costly job to do replacing certs. “eMudhra is working directly with customers who may be affected to give them replacement certificates, so that critical services are not disrupted. The company is also working with the root programs and continues its root-cause investigation,” the statement adds. The company allows that the incident “may have some reputational risks on eMudhra which cannot be quantified.” Ya think? ®

item.title: Ebola Case: Keyamo Orders 21-Day No-Fly Restriction For 46 Contacts
item.description: In a measure to contain the spread of the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) following a confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, said he has directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to place 46 persons identified as contacts of an Ebola-affected patient on a no-fly list for at least 21 days. The minister disclosed the directives in a statement posted on his verified X account following a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate. Keyamo said he has also ordered FAAN to strengthen Ebola surveillance and response protocols across all international airports, including enhanced health screening, temperature checks and travel history monitoring. According to Keyamo, the health minister provided a list of 44 persons who came into contact with an affected female patient at a hospital after she developed symptoms of Ebola, alongside two members of her domestic staff. “This evening, I held a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate over the Ebola scourge,” Keyamo stated. “He shared with me a list of 44 persons with whom the affected person came in contact at the hospital when she had developed the symptoms and an additional two persons who are her domestic staff.” He explained that aviation authorities were required to prevent the individuals from travelling by air for at least 21 days, corresponding to the period within which Ebola symptoms may develop following exposure. “Whilst efforts are ongoing to isolate them for now until there is certainty they had not been infected with the virus, the Aviation authorities are required to put them on a no-fly list for at least 21 days (which is the period that the symptoms are normally expected to manifest),” he said. Keyamo disclosed that he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to immediately notify domestic and international airlines of the restriction. “I have therefore directed the NCAA to immediately inform all local and international airlines of this development,” he stated. Photo illustration of Aviation Minister, Festus Keyamo, and an airport. The minister also instructed FAAN to intensify health surveillance and Ebola response measures at international airports nationwide. According to him, the airport authority has already introduced enhanced health screening, temperature checks, travel history tracking and digital health declarations. “I have also directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports,” he said. “Measures already being implemented by FAAN include enhanced health screenings, temperature checks, travel history tracking, digital health declarations, and strict inter-agency coordination with the NCDC following regional outbreak alerts earlier.” The minister’s statement did
