item.content:encoded: In a measure to contain the spread of the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) following a confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, said he has directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to place 46 persons identified as contacts of an Ebola-affected patient on a no-fly list for at least 21 days. The minister disclosed the directives in a statement posted on his verified X account following a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate. Keyamo said he has also ordered FAAN to strengthen Ebola surveillance and response protocols across all international airports, including enhanced health screening, temperature checks and travel history monitoring. According to Keyamo, the health minister provided a list of 44 persons who came into contact with an affected female patient at a hospital after she developed symptoms of Ebola, alongside two members of her domestic staff. “This evening, I held a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate over the Ebola scourge,” Keyamo stated. “He shared with me a list of 44 persons with whom the affected person came in contact at the hospital when she had developed the symptoms and an additional two persons who are her domestic staff.” He explained that aviation authorities were required to prevent the individuals from travelling by air for at least 21 days, corresponding to the period within which Ebola symptoms may develop following exposure. “Whilst efforts are ongoing to isolate them for now until there is certainty they had not been infected with the virus, the Aviation authorities are required to put them on a no-fly list for at least 21 days (which is the period that the symptoms are normally expected to manifest),” he said. Keyamo disclosed that he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to immediately notify domestic and international airlines of the restriction. “I have therefore directed the NCAA to immediately inform all local and international airlines of this development,” he stated. Photo illustration of Aviation Minister, Festus Keyamo, and an airport. The minister also instructed FAAN to intensify health surveillance and Ebola response measures at international airports nationwide. According to him, the airport authority has already introduced enhanced health screening, temperature checks, travel history tracking and digital health declarations. “I have also directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports,” he said. “Measures already being implemented by FAAN include enhanced health screenings, temperature checks, travel history tracking, digital health declarations, and strict inter-agency coordination with the NCDC following regional outbreak alerts earlier.” The minister’s statement did not identify the affected patient, disclose the location of the hospital where the contacts occurred or specify whether the infection was contracted within Nigeria. It also did not indicate that any of the 46 identified contacts had tested positive for Ebola. FAAN Heightens Vigilance Across Airports The development came after FAAN, on Wednesday, said it was maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations. It said it is working with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Port Health Services, Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and other relevant agencies to support ongoing containment efforts. The agency stated that early identification of the case and commencement of contact tracing underscore the importance of established public health protocols, effective surveillance and inter-agency collaboration in responding to potential health threats. “FAAN is maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations and will continue to coordinate with public health authorities, align its response with further guidance and support additional measures considered necessary to safeguard passengers, airport personnel and the wider public,” it said in a statement by the Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Henry Agbebire. It urged passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials. “The public is also advised to rely on verified information and avoid spreading unconfirmed reports,” it added. “FAAN reassures the travelling public of its continued readiness to work with relevant agencies to protect public health and support the safe operation of Nigeria’s airports.” The Federal Government confirmed a case of the virus in the FCT on Wednesday. This combo photo shows NCDC officials on duty in Nigeria, and response team members helping to wear protective suits before burying a person suspected of having died from Ebola in Bunia, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, on May 25, 2026. (Channels TV/GLODY MURHABAZI / AFP). FG Assures Nigerians Of Containment Strategies The Presidential Task Force on Ebola Preparedness, Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats has assured Nigerians it can handle Ebola in the country. The Chairman of the Task Force and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, said this while speaking to newsmen after the group’s emergency meeting at the State House on Wednesday. Gbajabiamila said the Task Force has been working behind the scenes since it was inaugurated in June this year. He added that this is why it was easy to detect the index case discovered yesterday. “It’s very important to note this. Since the issue of Ebola came up in June, there have been about 44, 000 flights in and out of Nigeria. So, it’s because of what the Ministry of Health, the task force and all the agencies have been doing. All hands have been on deck. “The passenger with the disease showed no symptoms, which came four days after the woman got into Abuja, and it was the identification process and the protocols that were put in place that enabled the quick identification. That also speaks to the country’s capacity and ability to deal with this disease as best as we can,” he said, according to a statement by presidential spokesman Bayo Onanuga. He assured Nigerians that the Task Force would strengthen whatever needed strengthening, the protocols, and ensure more rigorous enforcement moving forward. “The Task Force is on top of it. NCDC is on top of it; everyone is on deck. We must build community trust and avoid panic, but it’s also important to state clearly that this is a collaborative effort between the government and the people. He appealed to all Nigerians to respond to calls for compliance for the good of all. Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate using a manikin the evacuation protocols of deceased victims of Ebola during a training by a medical charity in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) at Ongata Rongai, Kajiado County in Kenya on July 10, 2026. ‘Nigeria Has Competent Health Authorities’ Meanwhile, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Ali Pate, said Nigeria has competent health authorities, including private hospital operators and agencies, Immigration, Aviation, Interior, and subnational actors, who have put surveillance systems in place across the country, ready to respond. “We have been conducting contact tracing diligently and isolating those contacts of the index imported case in this country. We will continue to do that, and we want to reassure Nigerians that the federal government, alongside its technical partners, the World Health Organisation, the Africa Centre for Disease Control, and our own Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, have activated the incident management system across the various pillars. “They are working day and night diligently, and our hospital cap

item.title: Cardoso puts Nigerian financial markets at centre of deeper investment ties with China
item.description: Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso has identified investment in Nigerian financial markets, including naira-denominated instruments, as a key opportunity to deepen financial ties with China. During discussions with the chairman and senior management of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), Cardoso outlined how greater participation by Chinese financial institutions could broaden the relationship between the two economies. He said Nigeria’s stronger financial foundations provided a more predictable environment for investment and enterprise. The priority was to consolidate stability and translate it into deeper markets, stronger investment and sustainable economic growth. “Our ambition is not simply to make financial transactions between Nigeria and China easier. It is to create the conditions for more transactions, greater investment and stronger financial flows in both directions,” he said. Cardoso identified greater participation by Chinese financial institutions in Nigerian markets as a practical opportunity to broaden the relationship. “We believe there is considerable scope to broaden this relationship, particularly by encouraging greater participation by Chinese financial institutions in Nigeria’s markets, including investment in naira-denominated instruments,” he said. The Governor outlined a role for ICBC in connecting its institutional networks with Nigerian investment opportunities. Its corporate relationships and international reach could help identify barriers to participation and translate commercial interest into financial activity. Nigeria and China already have substantial commercial ties. Cardoso said CBN data showed significant trade-related payments from Nigeria to China, alongside comparatively limited export proceeds and investment flows into Nigeria. Broader financial-market participation would add an investment dimension to a relationship heavily shaped by trade payments. Cardoso also set out the CBN’s responsibility: maintaining a credible, transparent and well-functioning financial environment, while working with counterparts to address regulatory and institutional barriers where appropriate. He proposed practical priorities and designated teams to carry the discussions forward. The measure of success, he said, would be greater transaction volumes, broader market participation and a more balanced financial relationship. item.title: Landing cost of petrol falls to N1,283.81/litre
item.description: •As crude oil rises to $108.90 per barrel By Ediri Ejoh The landing cost of imported Premium Motor Spirit, PMS, also known as petrol, has dropped marginally to N1,283.81 per litre from N1,292.88 per litre. The latest figure was disclosed by the Major Energies Marketers Association of Nigeria, MEMAN, in its energy bulletin yesterday. The decline came as Brent crude rose marginally to $108.90 per barrel from $108.80 per barrel, according to figures contained in the report. The latest landing cost is N66.19, or about 4.90 per cent, below Dangote Refinery’s gantry price of N1,350 per litre. Similarly, the landing cost of imported petrol was between N64.19 and N74.19 per litre below the ex-depot prices of N1,348 to N1,358 quoted by depot owners. Despite the decline in landing cost, petrol prices remained elevated in parts of the country, with motorists in Lagos and Abuja reportedly paying between N1,370 and N1,429 per litre at filling stations. The difference between landing costs and pump prices reflects additional costs and margins across the supply chain, including transportation, storage and retail operations. The development comes amid the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day petrol discount at NNPC Limited filling stations. Recall that the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, on October 8 proposed that petrol be sold at N1,350 per litre at NNPC Limited outlets under the planned discount initiative. However, the proposed discount had yet to be implemented at NNPC Limited filling stations as of the time of reporting. The post Landing cost of petrol falls to N1,283.81/litre appeared first on Vanguard News .

The development comes amid the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day petrol discount at NNPC Limited filling stations. Recall that the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, on October 8 proposed that petrol be sold at N1,350 per litre at NNPC Limited outlets under the planned discount initiative. However, the proposed discount had yet to be implemented at NNPC Limited filling stations as of the time of reporting. The post Landing cost of petrol falls to N1,283.81/litre appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Atiku lacks expertise to fix Nigeria’s economy — APC National Secretary
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ajibola Bashiru, has questioned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s expertise to fix Nigeria’s economy, saying President Bola Tinubu is addressing the country’s economic challenges while predicting that Nigerians will reject Atiku in the 2027 presidential election. Bashiru spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, while responding to questions about Atiku’s political ambitions and whether the former vice-president poses a threat to the ruling party ahead of the 2027 general election. “Atiku is not a professional, please, with respect to him. Atiku trained as an hygiene expert at the school of hygiene in Kano, He is a ‘wole wole’ man and went to be a tax collector in Customs. Where is the expertise? What has he done? Check his profile?” Bashiru said. He argued that holding the office of vice-president did not automatically make Atiku an expert on the economy. “So, the fact that you became a Vice President doesn’t make you an expert, what is his expertise?” he asked. Bashiru also linked Atiku to the economic difficulties the Tinubu administration is addressing, arguing that the former vice-president was among those responsible for the challenges facing the country. “If there are challenges that is being addressed by President Tinubu, one of the main people that caused it is Atiku Abubakar,” he said. Asked whether Atiku posed a threat to the APC, Bashiru described the former vice-president’s latest presidential ambition as his final attempt, predicting that Nigerians would reject him. “Atiku is the Oginga Odinga of our country and that is what the Vice president said. He is doing his last contest which he knows that Nigeria people would reject him because Atiku you mentioned cannot even come to talk about Nigerian economy,” he said. The APC national secretary also criticised opposition figures making promises about reducing petrol prices, arguing that such claims were unrealistic and intended to win votes. “You see, some of these people can just come to make statements. I learnt one of them said I’m going to make petrol 200 naira, 300 naira. It is not possible, he is just lying. You must not lie to people because you want to get their votes. You must even say something that is even realistic,” Bashiru added. The post 2027: Atiku lacks expertise to fix Nigeria’s economy — APC National Secretary appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Stop reacting, start protecting: Inside Nigeria’s fight to keep children safe in schools
item.description: By Adesina Wahab, Elizabeth Osayande & Ifunanya Ndigwe When a child leaves home in the morning with a school bag strapped to his back, the unspoken promise is simple: he will learn, grow, and return home safely. In Nigeria today, that promise is broken too often. •From left, President, All Nigeria Confederation of Principals of Secondary Schools (ANCOPSS), Lagos State, Mr. Olushola Masheyi walls,” she said.By 2021, the Ministry of Finance (representing ANCOPSS National President, Dr Robert Okorie); Executive Director, Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism, convened a high-level meeting Mrs Alaka; Chairman, Education Writers’ Association of Nigeria (EWAN), Mr. Mojeed Alabi; Lagos State Police Commissioner, Mr Fatai with Defence, Police, DSS, Office Tijani (representing Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu); National Coordinator, Financing Safe Schools in Nigeria, Hajia Haliof the National Security Adviser, ma Iliya and Chairman, Nigeria Union of Teachers, Lagos State Wing, Comrade Hassan Akintoye (representing NUT National President, Mr. Titus Amba) at the 2026 EWAN National Summit on School Safety in Lagos From Chibok in 2014 where schoolgirls were taken from their dormitories, to Dapchi, to Oriire in Oyo State, to corps members attacked in Imo, to classrooms emptied by sit-at-home order in the South-East and farmer-herder clashes in Benue, Oyo and Ogun – the classroom has become a frontline. It was against this sobering reality that journalists, security chiefs, government officials, teachers and principals converged on Ikeja, Lagos, for the 7th Annual Summit of the Education Writers Association of Nigeria, EWAN. The theme was deliberate and urgent: School Under Threat: From Reactive Responses to Sustainable Protection. Chairing the summit was the Chairman, Governing Board of the National Universities Commission, NUC, Prof. Oluwatoyin Ogundipe, represented by Prof. Joseph Awoyinfa. The keynote, on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu, was delivered by the Lagos State Commissioner of Police, Mr. Fatai Tijani. But beyond titles and protocol, the message was one: Nigeria must stop waiting for the next abduction before it acts. The Chairperson’s Warning: Don’t stop at the press statement. Prof. Ogundipe, as chairperson, set the tone. He did not want another conference of communiques. He challenged education journalists to change the way school safety is reported. “When authorities announce new security measures, our reporting should not end with the announcement. When funds are allocated, we should investigate whether they are used as intended, and when investigations produce recommendations, we should return to determine what has changed,” he said. “Our ultimate objective is not to embarrass institutions. It is to ensure that they fulfil their responsibilities.” For a country where security votes and intervention funds often disappear into vague budget lines, it was a pointed call for accountability journalism

item.content:encoded: By Adesina Wahab, Elizabeth Osayande & Ifunanya Ndigwe When a child leaves home in the morning with a school bag strapped to his back, the unspoken promise is simple: he will learn, grow, and return home safely. In Nigeria today, that promise is broken too often. •From left, President, All Nigeria Confederation of Principals of Secondary Schools (ANCOPSS), Lagos State, Mr. Olushola Masheyi walls,” she said.By 2021, the Ministry of Finance (representing ANCOPSS National President, Dr Robert Okorie); Executive Director, Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism, convened a high-level meeting Mrs Alaka; Chairman, Education Writers’ Association of Nigeria (EWAN), Mr. Mojeed Alabi; Lagos State Police Commissioner, Mr Fatai with Defence, Police, DSS, Office Tijani (representing Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu); National Coordinator, Financing Safe Schools in Nigeria, Hajia Haliof the National Security Adviser, ma Iliya and Chairman, Nigeria Union of Teachers, Lagos State Wing, Comrade Hassan Akintoye (representing NUT National President, Mr. Titus Amba) at the 2026 EWAN National Summit on School Safety in Lagos From Chibok in 2014 where schoolgirls were taken from their dormitories, to Dapchi, to Oriire in Oyo State, to corps members attacked in Imo, to classrooms emptied by sit-at-home order in the South-East and farmer-herder clashes in Benue, Oyo and Ogun – the classroom has become a frontline. It was against this sobering reality that journalists, security chiefs, government officials, teachers and principals converged on Ikeja, Lagos, for the 7th Annual Summit of the Education Writers Association of Nigeria, EWAN. The theme was deliberate and urgent: School Under Threat: From Reactive Responses to Sustainable Protection. Chairing the summit was the Chairman, Governing Board of the National Universities Commission, NUC, Prof. Oluwatoyin Ogundipe, represented by Prof. Joseph Awoyinfa. The keynote, on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu, was delivered by the Lagos State Commissioner of Police, Mr. Fatai Tijani. But beyond titles and protocol, the message was one: Nigeria must stop waiting for the next abduction before it acts. The Chairperson’s Warning: Don’t stop at the press statement. Prof. Ogundipe, as chairperson, set the tone. He did not want another conference of communiques. He challenged education journalists to change the way school safety is reported. “When authorities announce new security measures, our reporting should not end with the announcement. When funds are allocated, we should investigate whether they are used as intended, and when investigations produce recommendations, we should return to determine what has changed,” he said. “Our ultimate objective is not to embarrass institutions. It is to ensure that they fulfil their responsibilities.” For a country where security votes and intervention funds often disappear into vague budget lines, it was a pointed call for accountability journalism. “Children are not safe until every school is safe” If Ogundipe gave the framework, EWAN Chairman, Mojeed Alabi, gave the conscience. Standing before his colleagues, Alabi began with a line that would echo through the hall all day: Children are not safe until every school is safe. “No parent should have to choose between a child’s education and their safety. No teacher should have to teach under the shadow of abduction, and no community should have to watch its future disappear because its schools have become targets,” he said. In a deeply personal address titled: Why Journalism Matters in the Fight Against Violent Attacks on Schools, Alabi traced the pattern Nigerians have come to know too well: an attack happens, government issues a statement, security agencies announce interventions, public outrage rises, then attention moves elsewhere – until the next attack. “We must therefore ask: how many more warnings, disrupted school terms and grieving families will it take before school safety becomes an unquestionable national priority?” he asked. His answer was journalism that makes the invisible visible. Not just reporting the number of children abducted, but asking whether the school had a functional emergency response system. Whether teachers had safety training. Whether there was a channel to report threats. How many school days were lost. Whether survivors returned to school. What support they got. “Behind every school attack are human lives. Children must never be reduced to statistics or used merely to provoke sympathy. Their stories deserve accuracy, dignity, sensitivity and appropriate protection of their identities,” Alabi said. “We cannot promise that journalism alone will end attacks on schools but journalism can ensure that warning signs are not ignored, public resources are scrutinised, failures are exposed, promises are tracked and affected communities are heard.” It was a call for newsrooms to invest in expertise, collaborate with researchers, and use radio, television, newspapers and digital platforms to reach communities often excluded from national conversations. The IGP’s Question: How can a child learn in fear? When CP Fatai Tijani rose to deliver the IGP’s keynote, he came with a question that silenced the room. “How can a child concentrate on learning when the fear of violence, abduction or other security threats is constantly present?” For IGP Tunji Disu, school safety is no longer a peripheral police duty it is national security. He outlined four pillars: intelligence-led policing and early warning, stronger police-community partnerships, improved preparedness and coordinated response, and professionalism with respect for human rights. And he had a warning for journalists too: “The need for speed in journalism must never displace the obligation to accuracy.” Sensational headlines, he said, can compromise rescue efforts and endanger children. The $15 Billion Question: Where did the money go? One of the most revealing sessions came from Hajia Halima Iliya, National Coordinator, Financing Safe Schools in Nigeria during the panel discussion. She took the audience back to the beginning how the Safe Schools Initiative was launched to enable victims to continue education unhindered, how persistent attacks forced Nigeria to sign the Safe Schools Declaration in 2019 alongside over 100 countries, mostly from the Sahel region and West Africa. “There is more to what we are seeing which requires collective collaboration. Some of the actors are cross-border actors. They pass through the land, through the walls,” she said. By 2021, the Ministry of Finance convened a high-level meeting with Defence, Police, DSS, Office of the National Security Adviser, Ministry of Education, NSCDC, governors, EU and World Bank. The verdict: Nigeria had no mid-term expenditure framework for school safety. “Under my leadership, we developed a national plan on financing safe schools 2023-2026. By 2022, this document was developed and was launched. We started full implementation in 2023, with the Federal Government releasing N15 billion to the implementing regions,” she disclosed. A database of vulnerable communities was built with CSOs, a National Safe Schools Response Centre established, and hunters, vigilante and forest guards trained within community ecosystems. Lagos and Jigawa, she said, have become champions. “Over 4,000 students were trained across four states last year,” she said, with technology deployed to communities without network and hardware for the Police Schools Protection Squad. Her plea: Governors must embed Safe Schools into annual budgets. Without a budget, there can be no sustainable protection. Fencing, data and a weak justice system The panel also brought the conversation down from policy to the school gate. Comrade Hassan Akintoye, Chairman, NUT Lagos Wing, representing the NUT National President, was blunt: school threat has always been around, but today it

item.title: Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers. Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said. Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20. “During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said. He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response. “Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said. The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting. “The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said. Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression. The post Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Insurance firms’ N300b stuck at CBN over verification for illicit funds
item.description: By Rosemary Iwunze Insurance companies are now struggling to have access to the new capital they raised, amounting to about N300 billion under the just concluded recapitalization programme. The funds were held in the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, pending verifications for illicit funds inflows. Vanguard learnt that following suspicion of possible illicit sources of some of the new investments in the firms the apex imposed stricter capital verification regime, a development which has proved tough for most of the insurance firms to scale through. It is further learnt that while the National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, has given approval for the apex bank to release the funds to the insurers, the affected firms are painstakingly going through the processes. Speaking to journalist during the virtual press briefing on the outcome of the Insurers Committee meeting, Chairman of Nigeria Insurers Association, NIA, Mrs. Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu, stated that, the insurance sector regulator has done its part while operators are currently working on the CBN criteria to access the funds on or before the end of this month. The insurers said they had planned to deploy the new capital in the third quarter of this year to boost their financial performance in 2026 while rewarding their investors with good returns in dividend for their support in the recapitalization program. Recall that the 24 insurance companies had cumulatively raised N300 billion during the exercise, added to over N700 billion existing capital, taking the total industry capital to N1.079 trillion, post recapitalisation. The Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA), 2025, had stipulated that the underwriting firms and reinsurers who participated in the recapitalisation exercise that ended on July 31st, 2026 must keep their recapitalised funds in an escrow account with CBN. Of the 50 firms that scaled through the recapitalisation hurdle, 24 of them raised fresh capital while 26 of them had earlier surpassed the minimum capital benchmark. NIIRA had mandated life underwriters to recapitalise from N2billion to N10billion, non-life from N3billion to N15billion while reinsurers were required to upgrade from N10billion to N35billion. The Commissioner for Insurance/CEO, NAICOM, Mr. Olusegun Omosehin, had earlier disclosed that the capital in the market has now risen to N1.079trillion, up from about N700billion before the exercise. According to him, NAICOM now wants to allow operators access the recapitalisation funds, he promised that the regulator would monitor the operators to ensure that the funds fulfill its purpose and not mismanaged or divested into something else. The post Insurance firms’ N300b stuck at CBN over verification for illicit funds appeared first on Vanguard News .

Successive dry summers and rising energy bills are increasing public scrutiny of plans for the huge computer warehouses that are used to train and run AI models, says a submission to the Labour government from a group including the AI infrastructure companies Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco. item.title: IBM CEO says open weight models are now irresistibly good and cheap on-prem
item.description: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna has told investors that open weight models now make brilliant sense for on-prem enterprise use. Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Krishna said that in 2024 closed frontier models were plainly superior to open alternatives. “If you ran some assessment, some benchmark, and it was broad-based, not narrow, the top model might score a 70, and the open model might score a 20 or a 30.” “In late 2025, we began to see that gap shrink, where maybe the gap was not 70 to 20 or 30, it was 70 to 50,” he continued. The CEO said open weight models currently deliver “anywhere from 25 percent to 10 percent of the token cost of the frontier models. That is very attractive given that they’re now 90 percent as effective.” “It’s a simple question for any enterprise. Would you like something that’s 10 percent of the cost if it’s 90 percent as good as the best, or do you want to pay that 10 times higher cost?” Krishna thinks businesses will most often choose not to incur the higher costs. “Then the question is: how many tasks require that? I would tell you some do, but the vast majority, summarizing an email, examining a contract, answering a customer call, composing an email, all of those can be done as well with the much cheaper answer.” The CEO said those numbers mean IBM is seeing booming interest in on-prem AI infrastructure. While he thinks most businesses can build useful AI infrastructure in just two or three racks, he feels many will struggle to get it running. “The question becomes: how do you do that?” he said. “The question that the enterprise struggles with is: ‘Where are my kernel engineers? Where are the people who worry about the underlying network? Who can make sure that the model is clustered on GPUs that are close to each other in network proximity? Who can make sure that you’re doing the right caching of results so you get an incredible response?’” He didn’t have answers, other than to say IBM will produce software that eases AI deployments. Krishna also predicted demand for on-prem AI will spur sales of Big Blue’s Spyre mainframe accelerator cards. The CEO said current-gen z17 mainframes have delivered $1bn more revenue than any previous model, and said Big Blue’s new rackable models delivered “the strongest midrange launch in IBM Z in nearly two decades.” Mainframe revenue, however, fell 20 percent – as IBM expects given it’s now 18 months since it launched the z17. IBM’s infrastructure revenue grew five percent year-over-year to $3.7 billion, much slower improvement than recorded by rivals Dell, HPE, and Lenovo. Software did rather better, scoring nine percent growth to reach $7.8 billion for the quarter. Red Hat was the star, growing eleven percent and increasing annual recurring revenue by 30 percent. Some of that future revenue is for Red Hat’s virtualization products, which have now won $800 million of deals, with a pipeline of a further $750 million. item.content:encoded: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna has told investors that open weight models now make brilliant sense for on-prem enterprise use. Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Krishna said that in 2024 closed frontier models were plainly superior to open alternatives. “If you ran some assessment, some benchmark, and it was broad-based, not narrow, the top model might score a 70, and the open model might score a 20 or a 30.” “In late 2025, we began to see that gap shrink, where maybe the gap was not 70 to 20 or 30, it was 70 to 50,” he continued. The CEO said open weight models currently deliver “anywhere from 25 percent to 10 percent of the token cost of the frontier models. That is very attractive given that they’re now 90 percent as effective.” “It’s a simple question for any enterprise. Would you like something that’s 10 percent of the cost if it’s 90 percent as good as the best, or do you want to pay that 10 times higher cost?” Krishna thinks businesses will most often choose not to incur the higher costs. “Then the question is: how many tasks require that? I would tell you some do, but the vast majority, summarizing an email, examining a contract, answering a customer call, composing an email, all of those can be done as well with the much cheaper answer.” The CEO said those numbers mean IBM is seeing booming interest in on-prem AI infrastructure. While he thinks most businesses can build useful AI infrastructure in just two or three racks, he feels many will struggle to get it running. “The question becomes: how do you do that?” he said. “The question that the enterprise struggles with is: ‘Where are my kernel engineers? Where are the people who worry about the underlying network? Who can make sure that the model is clustered on GPUs that are close to each other in network proximity? Who can make sure that you’re doing the right caching of results so you get an incredible response?’” He didn’t have answers, other than to say IBM will produce software that eases AI deployments. Krishna also predicted demand for on-prem AI will spur sales of Big Blue’s Spyre mainframe accelerator cards. The CEO said current-gen z17 mainframes have delivered $1bn more revenue than any previous model, and said Big Blue’s new rackable models delivered “the strongest midrange launch in IBM Z in nearly two decades.” Mainframe revenue, however, fell 20 percent – as IBM expects given it’s now 18 months since it launched the z17. IBM’s infrastructure revenue grew five percent year-over-year to $3.7 billion, much slower improvement than recorded by rivals Dell, HPE, and Lenovo. Software did rather better, scoring nine percent growth to reach $7.8 billion for the quarter. Red Hat was the star, growing eleven percent and increasing annual recurring revenue by 30 percent. Some of that future revenue is for Red Hat’s virtualization products, which have now won $800 million of deals, with a pipeline of a further $750 million. That’s a solid result for a product line launched in 2024, and IBM believes there’s more to come given the possibility some VMware users are on the move. Total quarterly revenue hit $17.1 billion, up five percent. IBM’s share price wobbled in after-hours trading and ended down a point or two. ‘Emergency maintenance’ for IBM Cloud Another IBM matter The Register is watching today is a severity one incident in the Big Blue cloud, caused by “emergency maintenance” that meant users could not provision new resources or virtual private clouds for 90 minutes. Users of IBM’s Classic Cloud, the service it acquired from SoftLayer in 2013, have been told Big Blue will “restore new provisioning and resource management in our Classic environment” by 08:00 UTC on Thursday – meaning the incident will last at least 16 hours. IBM commenced that work a handful of hours after the announcement of critical bugs in PHP . We’ve asked if fixing that flaw is the reason for the incident and will update this story if we get a response. ®

item.title: APOD: 2026 October 22 – The First Green Star, WD J1330+6435
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 22 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The First Green Star, WD J1330+6435 Explanation: Star light, star bright: is there a green star out tonight? Other than the Sun , all stars are so far from Earth that they appear as points in the sky. They are mostly white, but sometimes noticeably red or blue . This color typically relates to the temperature: blue stars are hotter than red stars. What about other colors? The featured image is an illustration showing WD J1330+6435 , a white dwarf star , surrounded by an accretion disk with gas and rocks orbiting the star. White dwarfs are small, faint stars that are left over when a star like the Sun exhausts its nuclear fuel . Astronomers recently found that some white dwarf stars, despite their name, would appear yellow, green, cyan, pink, or purple . In these cases , trace elements that were accreted to these stars interact with the stellar atmosphere and shift its normally white color. But, alas! I wish I may, I wish I might, but they are too faint to see tonight … Tomorrow’s picture: eye in the sky Date October 22, 2026 Credit & Copyright Mark A. item.title: All party members in Final Fantasy Resonance
item.description: Meeting new party members in Final Fantasy Resonance is part of the journey. As in other games in the series, you start with only a few characters who team up to go on an adventure, but as they progress, they make friends who join the group. Although you can only use up to four characters in combat, unlocking all available party members broadens your strategic options.

item.title: Where to find all ancient equipment in Final Fantasy Resonance
item.description: As you progress further in Final Fantasy Resonance , you'll start stumbling upon ancient items , whether they're types of armor or weapons. At first, their stats will be laughably low (literally sitting at one for their respective stats), but certainly there's more to these equips that meets the eye. Yes! You can upgrade the ancient items into some of the best equips in the game , provided you can take on a few tough enemies.

item.description: As you play Final Fantasy Resonance , you may be wondering where Sephiroth's Vision is. You can see it in the menu, greyed out, and certainly the iconic antagonist from Final Fantasy 7 wouldn't just be found in a shrine like the rest of the Visions from other games. Well, you're right. Sephiroth is somewhat hidden, though to unlock him, you'll need to actually defeat him as a boss.

But in September and October 2026, as drought gripped New Guinea (sometimes called Papua) amid a strong El Niño , fires scorched the island and smoke shrouded large swaths of it for weeks. The VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) on the NOAA-20 satellite captured this image of thick smoke streaming from the southern part of the island on October 11, 2026. In recent weeks, soaring levels of air pollution delayed and canceled flights , closed schools, and prompted officials in some areas to urge children and older people to wear masks. “Sometimes smoke that has drifted into the convection of nearby thunderstorms will get washed out or lofted up into the upper troposphere, but a lot of smoke stays near the surface and causes air quality problems,” said Robert Field, an associate research scientist at NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies and Columbia University. “It’s a horrible situation.” According to the Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED), a fire emissions monitoring system, fires in Papua New Guinea, on the eastern half of the island, had released nearly 32 megatons of carbon by October 19, more than any other year on record at that point in the year. “Emissions are already much higher than the 2015 total for the year, and it’s very likely that this will become the highest year on record for Papua New Guinea, even surpassing 1997,” said Guido van der Werf, a fire scientist at Wageningen University & Research. On the Indonesian side, sometimes called West New Guinea or Indonesian Papua, carbon emissions exceeded 35 megatons , the third highest after 2015 and 1997, other El Niño years with severe fires. Van der Werf led the development of GFED, a satellite-driven modeling framework that uses a mix of remote sensing , vegetation characteristics, and other information to estimate the extent of vegetation fires and the emissions over nearly three decades. item.content:encoded: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Fires Char New Guinea Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search New Guinea, the world’s second-largest island, harbors an extraordinary variety of plant life across more than a dozen distinct ecoregions , including seasonally dry savannas, tropical rainforests, and lowland swamp forests. But in September and October 2026, as drought gripped New Guinea (sometimes called Papua) amid a strong El Niño , fires scorched the island and smoke shrouded large swaths of it for weeks. The VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) on the NOAA-20 satellite captured this image of thick smoke streaming from the southern part of the island on October 11, 2026. In recent weeks, soaring levels of air pollution delayed and canceled flights , closed schools, and prompted officials in some areas to urge children and older people to wear masks. “Sometimes smoke that has drifted into the convection of nearby thunderstorms will get washed out or lofted up into the upper troposphere, but a lot of smoke stays near the surface and causes air quality problems,” said Robert Field, an associate research scientist at NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies and Columbia University. “It’s a horrible situation.” According to the Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED), a fire emissions monitoring system, fires in Papua New Guinea, on the eastern half of the island, had released nearly 32 megatons of carbon by October 19, more than any other year on record at that point in the year. “Emissions are already much higher than the 2015 total for the year, and it’s very likely that this will become the highest year on record for Papua New Guinea, even surpassing 1997,” said Guido van der Werf, a fire scientist at Wageningen University & Research. On the Indonesian side, sometimes called West New Guinea or Indonesian Papua, carbon emissions exceeded 35 megatons , the third highest after 2015 and 1997, other El Niño years with severe fires. Van der Werf led the development of GFED, a satellite-driven modeling framework that uses a mix of remote sensing , vegetation characteristics, and other information to estimate the extent of vegetation fires and the emissions over nearly three decades. Unusually dry weather—a byproduct of El Niño shifting rainfall patterns —has primed ecosystems across the island to burn. The southernmost part of Papua New Guinea, dominated by relatively fire-prone savannas and grasslands of the Trans-Fly region , went more than 90 consecutive days without rain, according to Papua New Guinea’s National Weather Service . Since August, parts of the region have seen precipitation of roughly 5 to 10 percent of normal, according to the weather service’s data. Local news outlets report that drought is causing crop failures , water shortages , and school disruptions . In this normally wet part of the world, people ignite the vast majority of fires, researchers say. Crop fires, pasture maintenance, deforestation and land clearing, and hunting are all common reasons people burn in New Guinea. In dry conditions, managed fires sometimes spread and burn uncontrolled as wildfires, particularly in the drier, southernmost parts of the island. “We’re seeing an exceptionally high level of fire activity in Papua New Guinea and Eastern Indonesia, particularly Indonesian Papua and Kalimantan, this year compared with Sumatra and other parts of Western Indonesia,” said Yang Chen, an associate researcher at the University of California, Irvine. “Papua has emerged as Indonesia’s new deforestation frontier.” Over the past two decades , land in Indonesian Papua has been cleared for industrial oil palm and pulpwood plantations, shifting small-scale cultivation, urban expansion, and mining . According to Global Forest Watch, the region lost 27,000 hectares of primary forest in 2025, nearly double the 2024 total and the most since 2017. Sumatra’s fires are relatively low compared to other drought years partly because many areas are already developed. “Areas with large oil palm, sugarcane, or pulpwood plantations also often have their own private fire brigades to protect their assets,” said Field. “It’s in unmanaged areas or primary forest edges where we’re generally seeing the most fire.” Researchers expect the fires to continue until the heavy rains of the wet season arrive in the southern part of New Guinea, typically in early November. item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

item.title: Philippine government suspends top tech official for alleged misconduct
item.description: The Philippines government’s Ombudsman has suspended a senior Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) official over allegations he assigned government contracts to a company he founded and continued to hold a stake in. The Ombudsman announced the suspension yesterday and named Undersecretary for E-Government David L. Almirol as the individual of concern, after considering “administrative complaints of Grave Misconduct, Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service and violation of … the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.” “In ordering the preventive suspension, the Ombudsman found strong evidence supporting the administrative charges against Almirol,” according to its announcement of the suspension. Almirol founded a company called Multisys Technologies Corporation that offers software development services, plus packaged products. After over a decade as the company’s CEO, Almirol in 2022 joined DICT at the request of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., to work on improving e-government services. The Ombudsman alleged that between 2023 and 2025 DICT awarded at least eight contracts valued at over ₱1.5 billion ($24 million) to entities linked with Multisys. The contracts covered information and communications technology consultancy, e-government application deployment, web-based messaging services, cloud infrastructure, data center colocation and software subscriptions. Evidence of those transactions is apparently on the record in Multisys’s books. Local laws mean Almirol should have divested his stake in Multisys within 60 days. The Ombudsman alleges the exec missed that deadline but later complied. It’s not alleged he issued contracts in the period during which he continued to hold Multisys shares. The Ombudsman has suspended Almirol without pay for six months, a step it says is necessary because if he continued in the role it “could prejudice the investigation, particularly given his control and custody of documents and evidence relevant to the case.” The org has also pointed out that its decision does not pre-judge the matter, but is “a precautionary measure intended to preserve the integrity of the proceedings and ensure an impartial and unimpeded investigation.” President Marcos Jr. made rooting out corruption a key plank of his platform and even created an agency to tackle the problem. However, it’s felt that some anti-corruption actions may have been partly politically motivated. Past tech-related scandals in the Philippines include a 2022 case that saw its Department of Education overpay for lousy laptops . ®

item.title: To help world gorge on GPUs, Nvidia brings cash bucket to fatten wafer-thin supply chain
item.description: Nvidia has decided that its future prospects rest on an improved silicon substrate and packing supply chain, so has dipped into its giant pile of cash to ensure it can get the parts it needs by ensuring its suppliers have the resources needed to play their small part in keeping the flow of GPUs and AI processors strong. It’s not unusual for manufacturers to invest in their suppliers, because it helps to create certainty and spread financial risk. For those deals to be announced at a major tech company’s conference – as Nvidia did at its Berlin GTC gabfest – is somewhat novel, suggesting the company feels the need to show investors it is working to ensure it can meet demand for its products, and that demand will persist for years. Several of Nvidia’s announcements pertained to silicon substrates, aka wafers. Whatever you call them, they’re blank, round, silicon slabs onto which chipmakers etch circuits. They’re made by companies that sell to foundries like TSMC and Intel, which then turn them into chips of various flavours. At GTC Berlin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang observed that demand for AI hardware is vast, but that “Capacity is the constraint.” Specifically, capacity for activities like building substrates, advanced silicon packaging, testing, and creating optical connectors. Big Green therefore plans to increase substrate capacity for its products by 2.5x over the next three years. To make that happen, Nvidia has added Samsung’s Electro-Mechanics business unit to its substrate supply chain. Samsung apparently has immediate capacity at a factory in South Korea and Nvidia intends to tap that now. The deal means that by 2028, about a quarter of Sammy’s substrate output will go to Nvidia. Nvidia already has a deal with Japanese substrate outfit IBIDEN. In Berlin, the GPU giant pointed to further expansion that will triple production at an IBIDEN plant. Taiwanese substrate player Unimicron is also benefiting from Nvidia’s generosity, in the form of a capacity reservation agreement and associated plant expansion plans. It’s not just wafers that Nvidia wants to tuck into. The company has also signed a capacity reservation with Korean silicon packaging player Amkor. Again, Big Green’s involvement will see its partner expand capacity, in this case by 300 percent. Nvidia says this deal “will support higher production volumes for current and next-generation platforms.” AI systems need speedy networks, and many players see optical connections as the best way to build systems capable of handling the data deluges modern workloads create and require. Nvidia has therefore hatched a plan to boost manufacturing capacity at optics outfit SPIL. Again, Big Green already has a deal with the company, but in Berlin it expanded that arrangement in the hope it expands production capacity 15x by mid-2027, then doubles that again by the end of 2028. All of which suggests that Nvidia believes the AI infrastructure boom has years left to run. ®

item.title: PHP blames supply chain security biz Chainguard for putting huge chunks of the web at risk
item.description: PHP developers have accused software supply chain security shop Chainguard of effectively revealing critical bugs in the open-source scripting language ahead of a planned official disclosure. On Wednesday, just hours after releasing emergency patches for the two bugs collectively called PHP2shell, PHP maintainers published a blog about how the vulnerabilities were found and fixed. They credited researchers at Calif, OpenAI, and Wiz with finding the security holes between August and September. All three companies have said they used AI models to find the vulnerabilities, which are now tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code on servers running PHP. This is especially serious because PHP powers huge chunks of the public web. It also adds a dose of irony to the “leak and disrupted disclosure” part of the blog, which blames Chainguard - a company that aims to secure software supply chains by hardening open source code - for the messy disclosure. The trouble, according to PHP developers, started on Tuesday around 15:00 UTC, when “two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media,” along with incorrect information about the release time and CVSS severity rating. At that point, no technical details leaked. The rumors, however, prompted PHP maintainers to warn people in advance about the critical flaws, and move the planned disclosure forward a day, from Thursday to Wednesday. “Distributors were still packaging the fix, so releasing immediately would have left many users without an easy way to update,” the PHP Foundation blog says. “Moving the release forward by one day was the best compromise between acting quickly, giving people time to prepare, and making sure everyone had a simple update path when the vulnerabilities were disclosed.” A couple of hours later, Calif “mistakenly” published a video showing a proof-of-concept exploit and “additional, though limited” information about the bugs, we’re told. “Mitigation advice we started providing to a few critical infrastructure providers around Oct 20th 23:00 UTC, may have leaked as well,” the PHP blog says, but it does not name these providers. And then it throws Chainguard under the bus: “On October 21st at 07:41 UTC, more than six hours before the coordinated release, Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo and published built images containing the fix. Like other distributors, Chainguard had received the patch in advance so its users could update the moment the vulnerabilities were disclosed. Any attacker could now study the fix in binary form while every other PHP user was still waiting for the release. This disregarded weeks of work by many parties toward a coordinated disclosure.” Chainguard CEO: 'We made the call' Chainguard CEO Dan Lorenc spoke with The Register on Wednesday, and while he doesn’t dispute the timeline, said his company "didn't leak." “These things are messy,” Lorenc said. Chainguard learned “something
item.dc:creator: Jessica Lyons
item.content:encoded: PHP developers have accused software supply chain security shop Chainguard of effectively revealing critical bugs in the open-source scripting language ahead of a planned official disclosure. On Wednesday, just hours after releasing emergency patches for the two bugs collectively called PHP2shell, PHP maintainers published a blog about how the vulnerabilities were found and fixed. They credited researchers at Calif, OpenAI, and Wiz with finding the security holes between August and September. All three companies have said they used AI models to find the vulnerabilities, which are now tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code on servers running PHP. This is especially serious because PHP powers huge chunks of the public web. It also adds a dose of irony to the “leak and disrupted disclosure” part of the blog, which blames Chainguard - a company that aims to secure software supply chains by hardening open source code - for the messy disclosure. The trouble, according to PHP developers, started on Tuesday around 15:00 UTC, when “two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media,” along with incorrect information about the release time and CVSS severity rating. At that point, no technical details leaked. The rumors, however, prompted PHP maintainers to warn people in advance about the critical flaws, and move the planned disclosure forward a day, from Thursday to Wednesday. “Distributors were still packaging the fix, so releasing immediately would have left many users without an easy way to update,” the PHP Foundation blog says. “Moving the release forward by one day was the best compromise between acting quickly, giving people time to prepare, and making sure everyone had a simple update path when the vulnerabilities were disclosed.” A couple of hours later, Calif “mistakenly” published a video showing a proof-of-concept exploit and “additional, though limited” information about the bugs, we’re told. “Mitigation advice we started providing to a few critical infrastructure providers around Oct 20th 23:00 UTC, may have leaked as well,” the PHP blog says, but it does not name these providers. And then it throws Chainguard under the bus: “On October 21st at 07:41 UTC, more than six hours before the coordinated release, Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo and published built images containing the fix. Like other distributors, Chainguard had received the patch in advance so its users could update the moment the vulnerabilities were disclosed. Any attacker could now study the fix in binary form while every other PHP user was still waiting for the release. This disregarded weeks of work by many parties toward a coordinated disclosure.” Chainguard CEO: 'We made the call' Chainguard CEO Dan Lorenc spoke with The Register on Wednesday, and while he doesn’t dispute the timeline, said his company "didn't leak." “These things are messy,” Lorenc said. Chainguard learned “something was coming in PHP” on Friday from one of the researchers that found the bugs, Lorenc told us. Later that night, using his company’s AI harness and a frontier model, the CEO and the Chainguard team independently found the same memory corruption vulnerabilities. All it took was a “basic prompt of ‘find bad vulnerabilities in PHP,’” Lorenc wrote in a subsequent LinkedIn post. On Saturday, Chainguard began working with the PHP maintainers, confirmed that some of its findings matched the bug reports, and helped test the patches. “The patches are crazy - this is not a simple vulnerability,” Lorenc told The Register . “It really did take them months to build a real, working patch for it. And then on Monday, the rumors started, and yesterday it just spiraled.” Some people published POCs on social media, other security vendors reported seeing real-world exploitation, and late Tuesday night Lorenc told us he decided to ship the fixes, and notified the PHP coordinated disclosure channel about his plans. “People were getting hit in advance” of the official PHP disclosure, “so we made the call to ship the fixes under that,” Lorenc said. “It's coordinated vulnerability disclosure, unless there's evidence of active exploits in the wild.” Also on Tuesday night, Chainguard published built artifacts and made them accessible to anyone, not just customers. “And then I woke up this morning and saw that this was all our fault,” Lorenc said. When asked if he would do anything differently, given the fallout from Chainguard’s early disclosure, Lorenc said no. “This process and policy is based on trying to coordinate as much as possible until shit hits the fan and people start weaponizing things,” he said. “It sucks, because we really are all on one team, and there's bad guys over there doing stuff.” Chainguard’s honeypots trapped IPs from China and Russia targeting the vulnerabilities on Wednesday, Lorenc added. “Just being told there's a vulnerability in a piece of software - even something as big as PHP - is enough to find it,” he told us. “I did that myself without any other knowledge on Friday." "I think this is kind of the new normal. People are able to build an exploit in hours without even knowing what the vulnerability is." What we know about the CVEs and how to exploit them While we still don’t know the scope of exploitation - or what will happen to vulnerable legacy systems that don’t have security fixes - threat hunters predict it’s going to be a doozy. “Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them,” Wiz researchers Sagi Tzadik, Shir Tamari, Nir Ohfeld, and Tomer Schwartz warned on Wednesday, adding the oft-quoted stat that PHP powers 70 percent of all websites in the world. “Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4,” the Wiz kids wrote. “Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised.” Both bugs are related to how PHP handles memory management and error handling, and both lead to remote code execution (RCE). They can cause a corrupted internal PHP state when a request ends unexpectedly, and then a later request can reuse that state, leading to memory disclosure or RCE. “Both are memory corruption vulnerabilities,” VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity explained. “If an attacker can shape the memory PHP trusts, they can potentially hijack what it does next, and in these cases that means remote code execution.” CVE-2026-109618 ( GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w ) leads to RCE via out-of-memory corruption. “If a request reached PHP's memory_limit at exactly the wrong moment, PHP could leave partially initialized internal data behind and later treat it as valid, corrupting memory,” the project maintainer wrote. “On Apache with mod_php, an unauthenticated request can trigger this before any application code runs.” CVE-2026-109619 ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ) allows RCE via stale state. “A fatal error at the wrong point could leave internal state pointing to memory that belonged to a previous request,” according to the PGP Foundation. “A later request handled by the same worker could then use that freed memory. A use-after-free and worker crash were confirmed, and the reporter demonstrated remote code execution against a real-world application running on Apache with mod_php.”®

item.title: The 10 best alchemy cards in Magic: The Gathering, ranked
item.description: Love it or hate it, Alchemy fundamentally expanded Magic ’s mechanical lexicon. It proved a digital platform that could just as easily test ideas physically impossible on cardboard as much as it simulated paper play. Drafting the Power Nine from thin air, altering card stats permanently across zones, and directly patching first-player win-rate disparities horrified MTG purists, yet it also gave digital players a hyper-evolving metagame that embraced software's speed.

item.title: ‘It doesn’t look good’: Arteta concerned as Saka limps off against Bayern Munich
item.description: ‘A player off with really sharp pain is never good news’ Winger forced off 10 minutes into Arsenal’s 2-2 draw Mikel Arteta made no attempt to conceal his concern over the quad injury that forced Bukayo Saka out of Arsenal’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich , saying it did not “look good at all”. The manager was delighted with the fight that his players showed, Declan Rice earning a deserved point with an 82nd-minute equaliser. Arsenal had led through Eberechi Eze, who came on in the 10th minute for the stricken Saka, before Harry Kane took centre stage. The Bayern striker set up Alphonso Davies for 1-1 before giving his team the lead from the penalty spot. Continue reading...

item.title: Sudan’s war escalates as UN warns of wider regional crisis
item.description: In tonight’s edition: Sudan’s brutal war continues to take a devastating regional toll, as a drone strike in Abyei reportedly kills 153 people. We speak to the UN envoy for Sudan following an emergency international meeting on the escalating crisis. Also, health authorities prepare to coordinate a response as Ebola cases emerge in Nigeria and rise in Kenya. Finally, ten years after Cameroon’s deadliest railway disaster, families of the 79 victims are still fighting for justice, saying their pain has yet to be acknowledged.

item.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
item.description: A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI. New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand - with gas turbines or renewable energy - will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim. Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all planned data center projects were to plug into … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: FCC chair warns media not to run the "fake polls" Trump keeps complaining about
item.description: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr today warned broadcasters about airing "fake polls," amplifying one of the many complaints that President Trump has regularly made about the news media. Carr's post on X said, "Many journalists and broadcasters have been amplifying or airing these Polls without regard to basic journalistic ethics and without informing the public that those Polls lack a scientific, accurate, or even real basis... Broadcasters are advised to avoid engaging in News Distortions or running Broadcast Hoaxes by airing Polls that would violate their regulatory obligations." Carr urged broadcasters to "provide their viewers with additional context and information about Polls they have covered." In fact, one small polling outfit was exposed as a hoax this week, and a similar incident occurred in August. News outlets have reported on these hoaxes, providing the very "context" that Carr said is needed. Read full article Comments

item.title: Broda Shaggi Reveals He Was Hit by a Stray Bullet in New Documentary
item.description: Samuel Animashaun Perry (Broda Shaggi) explains the stray bullet incident behind his months-long hiatus in a new video. If you are a fan of Broda Shaggi ‘s skits, his music, or even just his lively presence on your timelines, you must have noticed that the popular entertainer and actor has been noticeably absent from social media over the past few months. Samuel Animashaun Perry has now officially returned, bringing along a deeply moving mini-documentary that breaks his silence and reveals the terrifying life-threatening ordeal behind his sudden hiatus . The multi-AMVCA winner revealed that his unexpected break was caused by a horrific incident where he was struck by a stray bullet while returning from a shoot. Recounting the frightening moment, Broda Shaggi shared,”We were done shooting and were on our way when we got stuck in a holdup. Suddenly, I heard a loud bang and everywhere went silent. I could see people talking, but I couldn’t hear anything. Then I touched my hip and saw blood. That was when it dawned on me that I had been hit by a stray bullet.” Broda Shaggi in an eccentric futuristic costume for one of his signature video skits. The incident led to an emergency hospital admission, extensive medical procedures, and an intensive period of physical rehabilitation . For a performer whose entire craft relies on boundless physical energy, comedy, and stage presence, being bedridden and unable to move presented immense physical and emotional hurdles . In the video, he candidly reflects on the overwhelming fear of losing his mobility and the uncertainty of how he would continue doing what he loves . Tracing his road from severe setback to resurgence, the documentary shows his gradual process of learning to walk again, moving from complete immobility to crutches and eventually regaining his strength . Now stepping back in front of the camera on his own terms, Broda Shaggi is turning what could have been a tragic end into a triumphant second chapter, ready to reconnect with his fans and dive back into his creative work . Watch below The post Broda Shaggi Reveals He Was Hit by a Stray Bullet in New Documentary appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Trump admin 'destroying' US democracy with 'autocratic, terrorist version of Christian nationalism'
item.description: François Picard welcomes former US Assistant Secretary of Defense Jim Townsend and former US Air Force officer Michael (Mikey) Weinstein, founder and president of the Military Religious Freedom Foundation. From the reported restrictions on Ukraine's access to Starlink satellite communications to the Trump administration's overtures towards Vladimir Putin and the growing controversy over religious ideology within the Pentagon, the two guests offer a stark assessment of the direction of American foreign and defence policy.

item.title: Xbox wants you to pay 24 to 40 cents per hour to stream games you already bought
item.description: In September, when Microsoft severely limited the game-streaming buffet available to Game Pass subscribers , the company said non-subscribers would soon be able to "purchase cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and stream eligible games they own on supported devices." Today, Microsoft rolled out those a la carte Cloud Playtime purchases to Xbox Insiders, with prices that might be a bit galling for players who have already purchased these streamable games. The "introductory launch pricing" for Xbox's Cloud Playtime purchases is as follows: 10 hours for $4 (~$0.40/hour) 25 hours for $8 (~$0.32/hour) 50 hours for $12 (~$0.24/hour) Purchased playtime "remains available until it’s used," Microsoft writes, so you don't have to worry about your 50-hour purchase expiring before you can use it fully. Read full article Comments

item.title: Enterprises keep buying software upgrades that IT thinks will make things worse
item.description: Enterprise-sized businesses spend, on average, 28 percent of their software budgets on unwanted upgrades, migrations, and licensing changes. Often, those firms' IT heads think those changes are detrimental. Those results are according to a survey of 2,018 chief information officers and senior IT decision-makers at companies with at least 10,000 employees that Origina commissioned for its report, “ The Software Tax .” About half of the respondents (1,011) are from the US, and the rest are from the United Kingdom. All respondents worked at companies with at least $1 billion in annual revenue. Keep in mind that Origina provides maintenance for various enterprise software. Its report points to independent software maintenance as a way for IT leaders to regain control over software budgets, illustrating its potential bias. A third-party research consultancy, Censuswide , conducted the survey. Read full article Comments

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
item.description: null On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year. The mission ended abruptly 14 months ahead of its planned end date when scientists lost contact with the probe . An Indian PSLV rocket launches the Chandrayaan-1 moon mission on Oct. 21, 2008 EDT (Oct. 22 local time in India). (Image credit: ISRO) Why it mattered The Indian Space Research Organisation , or ISRO, had a lot riding on the success of Chandrayaan-1 moon mission, which marked the first-ever deep space mission by the Indian space agency. It was also the first mission to the moon for India, a country that hopes to launch its own crewed spacecraft and build a space station. Chandrayaan-1 did more than just demonstrate that India's space program was capable of launching missions to the moon; it also returned some amazing science results, like evidence of water ice on the moon . "In September 2009, scientists published results of data collected by the American M3 instrument which had detected absorption features on the polar regions of the surface of the Moon usually linked to hydroxyl- and/ or water-bearing molecules," NASA said in a mission overview . The spacecraft carried 11 instruments to study the moon, five of them built by ISRO. The rest were experiments for the European Space Agnecy and NASA. "In addition to the five Indian instruments, the spacecraft carried scientific equipment from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Sweden, and Bulgaria," NASA said. It took until Nov. 8, 2008 for Chandrayaan-1 to enter lunar orbit, where it stayed until contact was lost in August 2009, most likely due to a power supply failure caused by overheating.
