item.content:encoded: Some photographs only reveal their true weight with time. A childhood birthday, a family Christmas, a traditional marriage or an old gathering can seem ordinary when the picture is taken, only to become more meaningful years later as the people, circumstances and memories around them change. That is what is beginning to emerge from Nigerian Breweries’ Together, Every Moment, as Nigerians revisit old photographs and videos and share the stories behind moments that once seemed routine. Across the entries received so far are memories shaped by family, growth, humour, loss and unexpected connections to brands that have been part of Nigerian life for decades. For content creator Virtuous, one of those memories came from a family gathering during her childhood. In the photographs she shared, drinks from Nigerian Breweries appear on the table, an ordinary detail at the time but one that would later take on a different meaning. Years after those pictures were taken, she went on to work with Amstel Malta , creating an unlikely link between a childhood memory and her adult career. “If you told the girl in the first and second slides that she would grow up to work with the brands she held in her hands as a child, she absolutely would have believed you. I always knew please ,” she joked. For Stella Ezenwata , the memory is tied to her traditional marriage in January 2017, an occasion she can now laugh about even though it felt far less amusing at the time. The marriage list specifically requested Star, Heineken or Gulder, but when a different drink was brought instead, the family insisted it be returned. Another item requested for the Umuada could not be found, leaving the couple to offer money in its place. “Honestly, the stress no be here,” Stella recalled. Nine years later, what was once a stressful part of the day has become one of the stories she remembers most clearly. Ralph ’s entry reaches further back, to his sixth birthday shortly after his family moved into a new home. The photograph shows children gathered indoors, some caught mid-dance, with bottles of Maltina visible in the foreground. What stayed with him was the excitement of marking his birthday in the new house, surrounded by family. It is the kind of childhood moment that can feel small at the time but grows in meaning with distance. For @ anna4manuel , that passage of time changed the meaning of her memory in a more painful way. She shared a Christmas video of her family dressed in red, gathered around a dining table and preparing for the festivities, with bottles of Maltina among them. Nothing about the footage immediately suggests why the moment has stayed with her so strongly. It looks like a familiar family Christmas, one of those occasions that can easily be taken for granted while everyone is still together. Her caption gives the video an entirely different meaning. “I didn’t know it would be my last Christmas with my father,” she wrote. What was once simply a record of a family celebration is now a reminder of a moment she can never recreate. The entries reflect how differently memories can age. Some become funnier with time, some take on new meaning as life changes, while others become more precious because of what came after them. The photographs may capture a single moment, but the stories around them often reveal much more. One of the most striking examples came not from a photograph, but from a comment shared during the anniversary conversation. Instagram user @dr_deraaa revealed that her grandfather, who turns 105 this month, spent 35 years working at Nigerian Breweries in Aba before retiring in 1985. Growing up, she said, the family often heard stories about his years with the company, memories he still cherishes and speaks about today. If the dates in her account are accurate, his career would have begun around 1950, only a few years after Nigerian Breweries was established. That connection offers a different perspective on the company’s 80-year history. For his family, the story is not only about the occasions on which Nigerian Breweries products appeared, but also about the working life of a man whose career became part of that history. It is this broader idea that sits at the heart of the National Story Collection. As part of Nigerian Breweries’ 80th anniversary campaign, Together, Every Moment, Nigerians are being invited to share photographs and videos that capture how the company, its brands and its wider presence have intersected with their lives over the years. Eighty selected entries will each receive ₦1 million. Actress and comedian Kiekie , entertainer Real Warri Pikin and Nollywood actor Odunlade Adekola are among those who have joined the anniversary conversation and encouraged Nigerians to revisit their own memories. But the strongest stories emerging so far are the ones that feel least manufactured: a birthday in a new home, a traditional marriage that did not go quite to plan, a childhood photograph that later came full circle, a final Christmas with a loved one, and a 105-year-old man still telling stories from a career that began more than seven decades ago. Together, they show why the most interesting part of a photograph is often not what appears in the frame, but everything the frame comes to mean afterwards. To participate, share a photo or video featuring a Nigerian Breweries product and tell the story behind the memory. Post it on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok or X, tag @nigerianbreweriesplc and use #NigerianBreweriesAt80 and #NBAt80, or submit directly Here . item.title: A Seat for You and Your Bestie: Brutal Fruit Brings Women Together at The Pink Table Milan
item.description: Brutal Fruit’s The Pink Table brought Pan-African competition winners, their best friends and guests from across Africa together in Italy, making friendship the occasion for an international escape. Some experiences are made better by the person standing beside you. A beautiful view becomes the place you both promise to return to. A song becomes your song. Before you have found the words, she already understands. And when something feels almost too good to be real, one look at your best friend is enough: can you believe we are here? Much of the joy of female friendship lives in that shorthand. There is comfort in being known, in having someone who understands your sense of humour and shares the memories behind it. Taking that friendship somewhere new adds another chapter to a story already in progress. It can also make room for other people to enter it. Brutal Fruit’s The Pink Table Milan began with that feeling and an invitation to let the circle grow. From September 25th, competition winners and their best friends from across Africa and Brazil came together against the backdrop of Milan Fashion Week and Lake Como. The invitation had a simple starting point: bring your bestie. The consumer winners earned their places through retailer competitions, with each invited to bring her bestie. The details shaped the experience from the outset. A prize for one woman became an occasion for two, giving each pair someone familiar to share the excitement with as they stepped into a wider gathering. Born in South Africa, The Pink Table has travelled from home to Paris and now Milan with female friendships at its centre. The trip brought African women into an international setting alongside guests from elsewhere in the world, with time to find common ground through food, fashion and music. Female friendships have always been at the heart of The Pink Table and in Milan, bringing a bestie meant arriving with someone who knew you, while joining women from other countries and backgrounds offered the chance to get to know someone new. The South African spritzer brought them together through experiences designed to give connection room to materialize. A table is a good place to start and the welcome meal at Nonna’s captured that spirit. Generous Italian food, conversation and laughter brought warmth to a new setting. Sharing a table gave guests time to settle in and form camaraderie, creating an easy introduction to the women around them. The food belonged to Italy, but the pleasure of getting to know someone over a meal felt familiar. Fashion gave the conversation another kind of spark. At Barbara Rizzi’s show, where Brutal Fruit was the official drinks partner, winners, besties and creators experienced the work of a female-led Italian luxury label known for its craftsmanship and bold contemporary design. The details shaped the experience from the outset. Born in South Africa, The Pink Table has travelled from home to Paris and now Milan with female friendships at its centre. The trip brought African women into an international setting alongside guests from elsewhere in the world, with time to find common ground through food, fashion and music. Female friendships have always been at the heart of The Pink Table and in Milan, bringing a bestie meant arriving with someone who knew you, while joining women from other countries and backgrounds offered the chance to get to know someone new. The South African spritzer brought them together through experiences designed to give connection room to materialize. A table is a good place to start and the welcome meal at Nonna’s captured that spirit. Generous Italian food, conversation and laughter brought warmth to a new setting. Sharing a table gave guests time to settle in and form camaraderie, creating an easy introduction to the women around them. The food belonged to Italy, but the pleasure of getting to know someone over a meal felt familiar. Fashion gave the conversation another kind of spark. At Barbara Rizzi’s show, where Brutal Fruit was the official drinks partner, winners, besties and creators experienced the work of a female-led Italian luxury label known for its craftsmanship and bold contemporary design. There were looks to admire and impressions to exchange, giving guests a shared experience to talk about beyond their own friendship pairs. Milan offered other points of discovery too. At Museo Bagatti Valsecchi, Renaissance art and antiques added another dimension to the city’s creativity. Alongside the fashion, these encounters gave women with different backgrounds something to discover together. Milan’s appeal was also its ability to create those openings: a new setting, a shared interest and a reason to start a conversation. Music made that common ground especially clear. A 19-member performance team led by pianist Julian Cohen brought songs including Coldplay’s “Viva la Vida”, “Bella Ciao” and Whitney Houston’s “I Wanna Dance With Somebody” into the experience. For guests who had not all arrived knowing one another, a familiar song offered something immediately recognizable to enjoy together. Brutal Fruit’s L’Orange Rossa , which was inspired by the Italian Riveria, added a flavour of the destination to the occasion. But the detail that held these different experiences together was the company; the best friend you came with, and the women you knew you had a reason to get to know. At Lake Como, the wider circle came together at The Pink Table itself. Around 75 guests from across the world including South African actress Siphesihle Ndaba , content creator and influencer Sni Mhlongo gathered at Villa Regina Teodolinda in Laglio, where sprawling gardens opened to private access to the water providing a romantic and intimate backdrop. Hosted by Italian actress Marina Valdemoro Maino, the occasion brought food, music and conversation into one setting. For all its beauty, the villa offered something simple; it gave women somewhere to gather and time to spend together. Besties could sit beside one another while becoming part of a larger table. The comfort of an existing friendship and the possibility of a new connection belonged in the same space. At The Pink Table Milan, female friendships were both the reason to gather and the starting point for new connections. Across countries and backgrounds, Brutal Fruit gave women the space to discover what they shared. Bringing a bestie was the beginning of the invitation. Making room for a wider circle was its promise. Because while the destination was Milan, the real currency of the trip was connection. item.title: Dettol Nigeria: Storytelling Wraps Up Challenge with 30 Winners
item.description: Dettol Nigeria has concluded its “12 Hour Protective Shield” storytelling challenge, recognizing 30 Nigerians for sharing personal stories about their experiences with Dettol Original Antibacterial Bar Soap. The Dettol Original 12hrs Protection Challenge ran from 13 July to 31 August 2026, and invited Nigerians to share personal Dettol stories ranging from childhood memories to family and personal hygiene routines. After the challenge closed, 30 winners were selected and rewarded with cash prizes for their entries. The challenge was part of the wider campaign for Dettol Original Soap, built around its 12-hour protective shield against 99.9% of illness-causing germs. Under the campaign idea, “ 12 Hours, Protection That Moves With You, ” Dettol highlighted the importance of consistent hygiene as people move through their daily activities. Beyond the digital campaign, Dettol brought the experience directly to consumers through in market activations across multiple states in Nigeria, combining product education and demonstrations with handwashing stations and consumer engagement. Commenting on the campaign, Boma Harrison , Marketing Director, Reckitt West Africa , said, “We were particularly pleased to give Nigerians the opportunity to share their personal Dettol stories and hear what protection means to them and their families. The stories shared through the challenge reflect the place Dettol has held in Nigerian households over the years, while reinforcing the importance of hygiene in everyday life. ” The campaign brought together digital storytelling, consumer engagement and on-ground experiences to reinforce Dettol Original’s role in everyday hygiene routines, while giving Nigerians an opportunity to share the personal experiences that have shaped their connection with the brand. item.title: Fashion Innovation Africa to Convene 300+ Stakeholders at Inaugural Conference in Lagos on October 22
item.description: Fashion Innovation Africa (FIA) 2026 will bring together more than 300 stakeholders from across fashion, finance, technology and government to examine the structures, investments and partnerships needed to build a stronger and globally competitive African fashion industry. Scheduled for Thursday, October 22, 2026, at Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, the inaugural business conference is themed “From the Atelier to the Economy: The Architecture Behind African Fashion”. Endorsed by the Lagos State Government, FIA 2026 will focus on the systems and capabilities required to translate Africa’s creative talent into sustainable businesses, jobs and wider economic opportunities. The conference will convene successful fashion founders and business leaders alongside representatives from government, regulatory agencies, financial institutions, technology companies, logistics providers and other stakeholders across the fashion value chain. By bringing these groups together, FIA aims to strengthen connections between the creative, commercial and institutional players whose collaboration is essential to the industry’s growth. The full-day programme will feature a Government Keynote, fireside chats with leading founders, three panel discussions and concurrent masterclasses. Discussions will address critical industry issues, including access to growth capital, local manufacturing, supply chain resilience, quality standards, technology, trade frameworks and access to international markets. Uche Ajene , Convener of Fashion Innovation Africa, said the conference draws inspiration from the growth of Nigeria’s music and film industries, which have built stronger commercial structures and expanded their global reach over time. “There was a time when Nigerian music and Nollywood had immense talent but were still building the structures needed to support their growth and global reach. Today, both have made significant strides in taking Nigerian creativity to the world,” she said. “African fashion has similar potential, but realising it requires more than talent and visibility. We need stronger systems for financing, production, distribution, standards and market access. FIA is bringing the key players together to help build that architecture and position African fashion for sustainable growth and global competitiveness.” Beyond the conference programme, FIA 2026 will provide opportunities for businesses and industry stakeholders to showcase solutions, exchange ideas, build strategic partnerships and explore commercial opportunities across the fashion value chain. Fashion Innovation Africa is an initiative focused on strengthening Africa’s fashion ecosystem by connecting the people, businesses and institutions that shape its growth. Through industry convenings, strategic collaborations and opportunities for knowledge exchange, FIA seeks to advance the infrastructure, investment and market access needed to build a more connected, commercially sustainable and

item.title: Companies rushed in on AI. Now some are pulling back
item.description: Rapid AI adoption left workers cleaning up a flood of errors and low-quality work Employers around the globe are grappling with the fallout from rushing to adopt fast-changing artificial intelligence tools. Meta has scaled back plans to axe staff and use more AI agents after the company found employees were spending more and more time cleaning up technical and security errors, Reuters reported . And after thinning its workforce, especially middle managers , in a 2023 efficiency push, the company is expanding its managerial ranks again, LinkedIn posts from workers show. Continue reading...

item.title: Desperados and Young Jonn Create a Cross-Cultural Anthem For Living In The Moment With ‘Let It Go’
item.description: From the infectious rhythms of Latin music to the unmistakable pulse of Afrobeats, Desperados and Young Jonn are bringing two cultures together on “Let It Go, ” a new track inspired by living in the moment. Some moments are best enjoyed without overthinking them: a spontaneous night out, an unexpected link-up with friends, or the song that gets everyone moving. Capturing this spirit of freedom and self-expression, Desperados has teamed up with award-winning Afrobeats producer, songwriter and artist Young Jonn for “Let It Go.” Produced by Yung Willis , the Grammy-nominated music producer whose production credits span some of the biggest names in African music. Having worked with notable artistes including Falz, Wizkid, Kizz Daniel, Davido, Niniola, BNXN, Zlatan, Patoranking and Ice Prince , Yung Willis brings his production expertise to the collaboration, helping shape a sound that connects global influences with the energy of Afrobeats. Rooted in the brand’s identity and association with self-expression, Desperados continues to find meaningful ways to connect with the younger audience through music, culture and premium experiences. With “Let It Go”, the brand is using music as a touchpoint between its Latin roots and the energy of Nigerian culture. At the heart of the collaboration is “ Guao Guao ,” the reggaeton track Desperados created in partnership with Venezuelan artist Micro TDH and Colombian producer Ovy On The Drums. Built around a sample of this unique record, Let It Go brings a Latin-inspired sound into Young Jonn’s style, creating an Afrobeats song that reflects Nigeria’s vibrant music and nightlife culture. “Let It Go” is more than a fusion of two sounds. It is an expression of the Desperados vibe, where music becomes a way to encourage people to loosen up and enjoy moments that make life memorable. By connecting the global influence of Latin music with Afrobeats, the brand reinforces its place through music, culture, and self-expression. Young Jonn’ s ability to reinterpret global influences through a distinctive Nigerian style makes him a fitting partner for this expression. Rather than recreating the original, he gave the sound a fresh identity, shaped by the rhythm and movement of Nigerian music. Whether it’s the rhythm that takes over the dance floor, an ordinary link-up that turns into a memorable experience, the song captures the freedom of letting go and being fully in the moment. For Desperados, the brand’s involvement gives the song a cultural expression, connecting its identity to a sound that brings people together, encourages movement and creates room for memories. From recreating dance moves to sharing interpretations through lifestyle content, fans can join the “Let It Go” vibe beyond simply listening. By connecting the global influence of Latin music with Afrobeats, the brand reinforces its place through music, culture, and self-expression. Young Jonn’ s ability to reinterpret global influences through a distinctive Nigerian style makes him a fitting partner for this expression. Rather than recreating the original, he gave the sound a fresh identity, shaped by the rhythm and movement of Nigerian music. Whether it’s the rhythm that takes over the dance floor, an ordinary link-up that turns into a memorable experience, the song captures the freedom of letting go and being fully in the moment. For Desperados, the brand’s involvement gives the song a cultural expression, connecting its identity to a sound that brings people together, encourages movement and creates room for memories. From recreating dance moves to sharing interpretations through lifestyle content, fans can join the “Let It Go” vibe beyond simply listening. Watch the official music video below Listen to “Let It Go” here . Ready to catch the vibe? Follow @desperadosng for more updates. item.title: Mark Your Calendars! Ecclesia Hills Church Announces 6th Ecclesia Word Conference, “Freedom in Christ”
item.description: Ecclesia Hills Church is pleased to announce the sixth edition of the Ecclesia Word Conference, themed “Freedom in Christ.” The conference will take place from Friday, 6th November to Sunday, 8th November 2026, at The Hall, 16 Musa Yar’adua Street, Victoria Island . The Ecclesia Word Conference has grown into a gathering where believers are taught, equipped, and stirred to live out the fullness of their faith. Last year’s edition explored the theme Custodian of Holy Oracles . This year’s edition turns to a question at the heart of the Gospel: What is freedom in Christ, and how can the Ecclesia arrive there? “This conference is crucial to bringing believers to the accuracy of freedom,” said Pastor Moses Ida-Michaels , Pastor of Ecclesia Hills Church. “Many people carry the name of Christ yet remain bound by religion, fear, habits, financial pressure, and generational patterns. This gathering is about seeing freedom clearly and walking in it. Together, we will hack the principles that bring true liberty to life,” he concluded. Conference Focus Across three days, sessions will address freedom in every area of life, including: Free a Generation: El-Shakar Freedom from Religion: Jabar Mckellar Freedom from Mammon: Chris Delvan Freedom in Illumination: Eva Dan Yusuf Freed Bloodlines, Cycles, Enchantments: Edem Julius-Cudjoe Freedom from Sinful Addictions / Fear of Consequence: Chris Delvan Free to Serve God’s Purpose: Chris Delvan Freedom in Innovation / Innovative Liberty: Moses Ida-Michaels (Host Pastor) Liberty Ideology: Edem Julius-Cudjoe Worship will be led by Hill Music and Moses Akoh , creating an atmosphere for encounter, response, and transformation. item.title: Apple AirPods 5 review: the best open-fit earbuds yet
item.description: Upgraded, cheaper AirPods have noise cancelling, sound and controls to rival many plugged-in buds but without tips Apple’s latest AirPods set a new standard for open-fit buds with upgraded noise cancelling that now rivals many plugged-in designs of the same price. The AirPods 5 have the same design the popular AirPods 4 offering an option for those that do not like silicone ear tips used by most noise cancelling earbuds. They come in two versions, with or without a wireless charging case and swipe controls, costing from £119 (€149/$129/A$219) – £10 cheaper than the launch price of their predecessors . Connectivity: Bluetooth 5.3, SBC, AAC, H2 chip Battery life: four or five hours with ANC (22 hours with case) Water resistance: IP57 (up to 1 metre for 30 minutes ) Earbud dimensions: 30.2 x 18.3 x 18.1mm Earbud weight: 4.3g each Charging case dimensions: 46.2 x 50.1 x 21.2mm Charging case weight: 32.3g/34.7g Case charging: USB-C or wireless (Qi or Watch) Continue reading...

item.title: Systolic style: meet the medical-grade smartwatch revolutionising blood pressure monitoring
item.description: An estimated one-third of adults in England have high blood pressure, with research showing that many are unaware of their condition. But thanks to the new Huawei Watch D3, monitoring blood pressure is easier, accurate and more stylish than ever Wearable technology has come a long way in the past decade. Take a look around at your colleagues, friends and family, and you’ll be hard pushed to find anyone not wearing some kind of health monitoring ring, watch or band – there are even tracking insoles and patches, too. These gadgets have myriad benefits – not least, allowing us more control and insight over our health and wellbeing than ever before. We’re able to monitor everything from sleep and stress to heart health and more, and the technology is becoming more refined and intuitive seemingly by the day. Continue reading...

item.title: Welcome home, Sophie Adenot
item.description: Video: 00:02:54 After 237 days and over 3,700 orbits around Earth aboard the International Space Station, Sophie Adenot is back on Earth! Following a handover to Crew-13, Sophie and her Crew-12 crewmates undocked on 7 October and splashed down off the coast of California the next day. Now back in Europe, Sophie will begin her post-flight data collection and rehabilitation while readjusting to life on Earth after the longest mission in space by a European astronaut so far. Welcome home, Sophie!

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Mac mini M6 review: truly mighty but now more pricey
item.description: Apple’s cheapest desktop computer is no longer a bargain but its newest, fastest chip makes it a pocket powerhouse Apple’s latest Mac mini brings real speed and power for far more than everyday tasks in a practically pocketable form you can fit almost anywhere. The impressive new desktop machine is the first to receive an update to Apple’s latest M6 chip while remaining smaller than a headphones box. It is the cheapest computer Apple sells with an M-series chip, but like every other memory-containing piece of electronics, it has been hit by RAMageddon , driving up the starting price to £899 (€1,049/$899/A$1,449) from the £599 or equivalent of its M4 predecessor. item.title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold review: the foldable with the best triple camera
item.description: Big screen folder with slick software and advanced AI is just like a regular Android when closed Google’s latest folding phone sticks with its tried and tested design of a traditional phone shape when closed and almost square when open, in the face of new competition from Apple’s squat iPhone fold . The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is Google’s fourth-generation folder and is still one of the only models with a full water and dust resistance rating similar to standard slab phones. It costs from £1,799 (€1,999/$1,899/A$2,799), which is £50 (€100/$100/A$100) more than last year as the pressure of RAMageddon continues to push up prices. Continue reading...

item.title: Pixel 11 Pro review: Google’s best pocket camera goes customisable
item.description: Solid battery life, snappy performance and quality software make for a great smaller phone with a killer camera Google’s latest Pro phone is out to prove it has the best camera on a smartphone while embracing customisation, allowing you to change the look and feel of your photos far beyond simple filters even if that means making them technically worse. The Pixel 11 Pro packs the best of Google’s hardware and software into a still-pocketable and easy to handle frame, instantly making it a contender for best smaller phone of the year. Screen: 6.3in 120Hz QHD+ OLED (495ppi) Processor: Google Tensor G6 RAM: 12 or 16GB Storage: 256, 512GB or 1TB Operating system: Android 17 Camera: 50MP + 48MP UW + 48MP 5x tele; 42MP selfie Connectivity: 5G, eSIM, wifi 7, UWB, NFC, Bluetooth 6, Thread and GNSS Water resistance: IP68 (1.5m for 30 minutes) Dimensions: 152.7 x 71.9 x 8.4mm Weight: 204g Continue reading...

item.title: Superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
item.description: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble Space Telescope image in the upper central region.

item.title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
item.description: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight.

item.title: Igniting Roman's Journey
item.description: Now on a three-month, million-mile journey to its final orbit, NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will soon reveal the universe’s darkest secrets. The mission launched at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Aug. 30 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

item.title: August Lunar Eclipse Rises Over Louisiana
item.description: A lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana. The lunar eclipse was visible throughout much of North and South America and part of Europe and Africa between Aug. 27-28. The Full Moon slipped through Earth’s shadow on Aug. 27, continuing into Aug. 28 for some parts of the world, resulting in the lunar eclipse. At maximum eclipse, the Moon takes on a dramatic dark, ruddy or coppery tint along the covered edge. New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Artemis III RS-25 Engine Processing: #3 Lift
item.description: Technicians prepare to transfer the #2 RS-25 SLS (Space Launch System) rocket engine (front) to the work stand with the #3 engine (back) for integration with the Artemis III core stage rocket on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. During Artemis III, the four RS‑25 engines will launch the Orion spacecraft and its crew of four into low Earth orbit, generating more than two million pounds of thrust at liftoff.

item.title: Intuitive living is the latest wellness trend – meet the new tech making it work
item.description: Wellness culture can be overwhelming, but a more fluid approach is emerging. Smart devices such as the Huawei Watch Fit 5 perfectly embody this shift in direction – whether you’re regularly sleep tracking or just occasionally using data to support your lifestyle When it comes to the world of health and wellness, it’s easy to suffer from information overwhelm. We’ve never had more access to data, research and expertise which, while valuable, isn’t always applicable to our own lives. What’s more, few of us have time to spend hours sifting through content to devise a personalised health routine, let alone work out if a “routine” is necessary at all. All this information and expectation can come at a cost: emotional strain, guilt and confusion about where to turn. Health and fitness then start to feel like abstract milestones that we’re blindly chasing rather than important components of our lives. Continue reading...

item.title: The story of ‘earvolution’: from ceremonial piercings to fashion-statement earbuds
item.description: For millennia, humans have been captivated by ear decorations. Now, earbuds not only connect us to the digital world, they also showcase our personal sense of style – and the HUAWEI FreeClip 2 is at the forefront of that development When we are born, a cry can let the world know that we are healthy and OK. When we first begin to talk, we learn to express our needs and understand the needs of others. As we grow older, we learn that the sound of a siren denotes danger, that certain notes swelling together create the sound of a favourite song which lifts our spirits, or that a warm familiar voice on the other end of the phone means our best friend has our back. Our ears give us grounding and clues: they are our maps of the world, guiding us towards truth, keeping us from harm, giving us a constant stream of sensory information. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row

Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
